review_text: [5/5] [Apr 22, 2022 from Google]: You’re slowly biting into a piece of Sambousek covered in Hummus, with some Hindbeh leaves in the mix… You close your eyes to savor the moment as you let the explosion of flavors invade you. A nostalgic Fairuz song is playing in the background, and a soft breeze is caressing your cheeks. Life is good. It’s especially good at Em Sherif where the culinary experience combines richness and delicateness, comfort and elegance, past and present. A word of caution: you may have to roll out of the place, as walking would be physically impossible after what can only be described as a gargantuan feast… So you may want to pace yourself. It’s a set menu that takes the stress out of ordering, and ensures that energy is re-directed towards devouring the meal. And it’s classically Lebanese, with the cold and hot appetizers, the warm main dishes, and the desserts, all with small refined portions. Everything was delicious but if I were to pick some highlights: - The minced meat Rkakat and Sambousek were so scrumptious yet delicate at the same time - The Kibbeh with yogurt is another hit. The flavoring, the umami, the freshness of the yoghurt…combine magically together - Then when you think you’re done… comes a pleasant surprise: A muffin-shaped puff pastry filled with rice, minced meat, chicken and a whole array of condiments (raisins, almonds, shaved carrots, peas), sprinkled with a cinnamon flavored gravy… Sort of a “Riz aa Djej” with a twist. You won’t know what hit you. And you might come back for a second, third, maybe even a fourth serving. - The desserts.. what a beautiful note to end this extraordinary performance on. The date and molasses cake might trigger a few inappropriate sounds of approval. The Mhallabye with the loukoum and biscuits will feel decadently sinful. It’s a beautiful experience. Yes your tummy will beg you to stop, but your your heart and soul will beg for an Encore…

review_text: [5/5] [Jun 10, 2025 from Google]: Babel Bay always delivers a polished and memorable dining experience. From the moment we walked in, the attention to detail was evident. The food, as always, was delicious. Even on a public holiday, the level of service didn’t drop—a rare thing in Beirut. And the small touches, like the presentation of the hot towels, continue to reflect the elegance and consistency that Babel is known for. If I may offer a gentle suggestion or two: • For raw fish dishes, a bit of ice underneath would help keep things perfectly fresh—especially during warmer weather. • And for the bread service, maybe consider placing the hot bread separately from any plastic-wrapped items, just to maintain that premium feel and avoid unnecessary contact with heat and packaging. That said, Babel Bay remains one of the few places where you feel every element is carefully thought through—and that’s why it continues to be a favorite.

Chicken liver 7. Spring rolls (were a bit late) They offered us some lentil soup prior to the food on the house! It tasted good. Everything was very well prepared and the service was great. The food all tasted amazing and even the sushi! We enjoyed our meal and were also offered coffee on the house too. I recommend anyone who is in the area to try it. It is certainly not “cheap” but the value and the overall quality is more than acceptable. Thank you!

review_text: [4.5] [8 years ago on Zomato]: A Historian Making History: Abdo Restaurant In the past 3 years, I've been to many restaurants, tried so many different kind of foods, was wowed and was disappointed, got my highs and took my lows, until yesterday: Away from sophistication & complicated menus, came a teacher, a history teacher: He gave me and my dear friend GSN a lesson of traditions, an old lesson, going back to our jdoudna all the way to our fast present in a timeline of delicious dishes, simple dishes, traditional dishes. I was already in my Pajamas when I got GSN's call: Marwan you need to come and try Abdo Restaurant with me. The ignorant that I was replied: what's that? He laughed and said yalla you have 1 hour to be in Gemayzeh. 8:30 sharp I was stepping inside of… oh a chalkboard, nice touch for a school teacher. It's a tiny place with 3 tables, however from the kitchen size, you could tell his business load is on delivery. I wanted to make a long review about Abdo Restaurant, but I keep get that urge inside me to cut the prose and focus on the food and talk about Abdo himself: That history teacher who was forced by life to quit teaching and follow a different path to make a better living, a path that led him to discover a passion: La Graine de Blé. Developing that passion led him better fermentation and bacteria, on a certain level, the history teacher became a chemist. A Chemist with a passion, the passion to make the best dough ever made, and lord is my witness he succeeded. I will skip the part where Abdo himself explains the process of slow fermentation to us and jump right into those amazing zaatar saj… the Zaatar itself is unique, of an ultimate quality, zaatar leaves, simple zaatar saj, that 24 hours later I can still taste in my mouth and feel the echoes of its vibes through my body… a simple Zaatar les amis… We tried over different wraps and saj that night, and while the chicken and steak wraps were very good, nothing could come close to the traditional items he served. The History teacher who turned chemist just turned Artist: A dough artist, a traditional saj Artist, Artist avec un GRAND A. We were done, GSN and I, however, Abdo insisted that we try the beid bi awarma. We were sincerely full mais on ne s'est pas fait prier pour ainsi dire… and good that we didn't: another simple dish, beid and awarma: amazingly simple, took us to new heights of flavor in its simplicity, I couldn't stop eating. I wanted to but couldn't, it was the perfect balance between fried eggs and an extremely well done homemade awarma. Oh and yes, I almost forgot, when you go there (not if cuz you have to) try 2 drinks: the laban ana zaatar and the beetroot & carrots. Faites moi confiance and try it. Came the dessert: Apple and Biscuit in a jar with cinnamon: let's just say that it beats any dessert served in gemayzeh and mar mkhayel hands down, and when we thought we reached the paroxysm of flavors, came the "ka2anna knefeh" a Osmalliye wrap filled with cheese covered with Ater… We both went out of words, all we could do is look at each other and smile, happy and amazed. It's just when we were leaving that we realized another important thing: despite all what we ate, we felt light. And that is all thanks to the dough made by our teacher. Lesson well learned Abdo, you reminded us that simple things are always the best, you took us back in time and brought us back on waves of flavors and passion. We wish you all the success in the world Gaston L'historien

review_text: [4.5] [8 years ago on Zomato]: Disclaimer: Have you ever tasted a Hamburger in a Kaake? Concept: Abdo is a former History teacher who, with time, discovered a passion for baking that resides deep inside of him. He then decided to pursue this passion by creating his very own “aged” dough, which is sugar-free, relying on the natural fermentation process of the yeast. Abdo’s dough needs around 24 hours to mature unlike the commercial dough which contains sugar to enhance the yeast’s feeding. Abdo stopped teaching history but history has never completely disappeared from his profession. Abdo processes a cozy venue with a simplicity that intrigues you first thing when you step into the restaurant. A chock board that lists the menu items and a counter behind which your food gets prepared on display, a couple of tables around which wooden chairs are placed, and the most basic and traditional tableware constituted of metallic dishes, glass jars for cups, metallic pans for plates, and guess what, their baskets are covered with papers that contain exerts from the history textbook. The whole thing tells a story on the behalf of M3allem Abdo which you’re lucky enough if you get to listen to its details from Abdo himself. Food: When science meets food, something like Abdo’s dough is created: a perfectly light bread that is easy to digest. This kind of bread is crafted with passion to meet high standards of production. I was surprised by the great taste of beef patty in a Kaake. That was something indescribable. There’s even a secret to the sauce which does not taste like your every day burger sauce but is still 100% Lebanese and homemade. The taste of the beef patty isn’t disguised in a sugar-loaded bun but rather in a light Kaake to make a magical burger! Thanks m3allem! I also tasted the Chicken Pesto wrap and this too was super special. It’s done with genuine Pesto sauce that is prepared in house. I couldn’t get enough of it! Also, don’t miss their sour Wild Zaatar saj and don’t miss the side Labne dip which is a mix of cow and goat Labne. Moving to desserts, Abdo’s creations are amazing! كأنها كنافة is going to become your next addiction. Even if you’re not a great knefe fan, you’re going to discover a new love: filled up with luscious cheese and covered with othmalieh. Ending up with it is a must! Don’t leave without trying it. Last but not least, if you’re craving a sweet indulgence, the Apple with Caramel is one great choice: a yummy mess of apples, caramel, cinnamon, and crumbs in a pot. Abdo restaurant is where you’d certainly feel at home; particularly in a house in the village where your grandparents reside. It’s so full of love and smiles. Recommended for breakfast, lunch, and a late night light dinner. I would like to thank the manager for his welcoming attitude, hospitality, good company, light conversation, and the smile that accompanied us from the moment we entered to the time we left. Thanks to M3allem Abdo for giving me the time for a small chat full of wisdom and genuineness. With love, Nour :)

review_text: [5.0] [a year ago on Google]: Located in the heart of Lebanon, Abou Sami offers a delightful dining experience that blends traditional flavors with a contemporary twist. The moment you step in, you’re greeted by a warm ambiance and friendly staff that makes you feel right at home. The menu is a testament to Lebanese cuisine, featuring a wide array of dishes that highlight the rich culinary heritage of the region. The hummus is a standout, creamy and well-seasoned, perfect for dipping fresh pita bread. If you’re seeking something heartier, their grilled meats, especially the shish tawook and kebabs, are incredibly tender and flavorful. Each dish is prepared using authentic recipes and fresh ingredients, which is evident in every bite. One of the unique aspects of Abou Sami is their attention to detail not just in taste but also in presentation. The dishes arrive looking as good as they taste, adding an aesthetic appeal to your meal. The restaurant also offers a variety of vegetarian options that cater to different dietary preferences, ensuring that everyone can find something to enjoy. Service at Abou Sami is exceptional. The staff is knowledgeable about the menu and can recommend dishes based on your preferences. Whether you’re a first-timer or a regular, you’re treated with equal care and attention. The pricing is reasonable considering the quality of food and service. It strikes a good balance, making it an accessible option for casual dining as well as special occasions. Another highlight is the dessert menu, which features traditional sweets like baklava and mouhalabieh that perfectly conclude your meal. Pairing them with a strong Lebanese coffee creates a wonderful finish to your dining experience. With a few changes , would definitely give it a 4+

review_text: [3.0] [a year ago on Google]: We visited Amavi on a Sunday for late lunch. The interior design was incredible, a truly stunning space. Our waitress however, while friendly, wasn't very familiar with the menu. There were several trips back and forth to the pizza manager, to clarify missing items, as she was not aware of why some things were unavailable on the menu. Drinks, however, were a bright spot. Their cocktail cart was a fun touch, and the drinks themselves were beautifully presented and inventive. Though, the "special Negroni" was a surprising detour from the classic, being much sweeter than expected. We ordered 2 pizzas and one pasta. To start off, the penne arrabbiata was incredible. The tomato sauce was superior, perfectly balanced and bursting with flavor. However, the pizzas, which we were particularly excited about (knowing Marc from Marco Pizza), were a bit of a letdown. We ordered the pesto burrata and a goat cheese and honey option. Both were plagued by an overly-moist dough, turning the pizza into a near-soup situation. We've had Marco's pizzas before, and the crust was always fantastic, holding everything together beautifully. Here, the exceptional ingredients like the burrata and goat cheese couldn't save the soggy base. It was too soggy to the extent that we had to use our forks and knives to eat the pizza. The service wasn't the strongest either. Empty plates stayed on our tables way long after we finished, and there was no inquiry about our experience or dessert, which was very disappointing. It felt like a missed opportunity, especially considering the beautiful gelato kiosk we noticed on the way in. We ended up skipping dessert at Amavi and going out for some gelato elsewhere. Overall, Amavi gets a 2.9/5. The ingredients were undeniably high-quality, but the service and the disappointing pizza dough brought the experience down. Hoping for a better experience next time! Food: 3 Service: 2 Atmosphere: 3

review_text: [5.0] [7 years ago on Zomato]: I craved for some pizza when I was next to this place. The shop is a mixture of a Bakery and a Snack. The decoration and general look of the place looks very old, you can even see it from black and dusty walls. I thought I would give it a shot. Took a look at the menu and saw the prices, so I decided to go with the large regular pizza which costs 8,500LL. I did not pay attention when the operator was making it, because If I did, I would have immediately stop him and change my order right away. Because once the pizza was ready and I was called, I was shocked by its size, which was small as a regular manoushe. 8500LL for a regular sized pizza and they call it large on the menu. So disappointed. The pizza wasnt half bad itself, but the size total killed it. They could improve on the way they communicate with customers as well, especially the bakery operator. ------Update----- After my review, management contacted me to inquire about my complaint. I've previously mentioned in many of my reviews before, that disregarding my initial complaint or dissatisfaction, if management of a certain restaurant calls me (or any customer) in order to follow up with my faced issue and try to solve it, then this restaurant gets my loyalty and utter respect, and my full 5 stars here on zomato. After explaining to me the pricing of their pizzas, which was based upon fresh ingredients used daily and especially on the cheese and sauce, which I do agree with them because as I've said the pizza itself was very good, it was just the size and the pricing that I did not agree with. So they offered me a complementary lunch, which they they didn't specify what it was, and I had to find out when I received it. It was a mix of chicken, sauce, melting cheese and green pepper and corn all filled in a closed and baked dough. It was very delicious, and after having it, I immediately went to read their menu to find out what it was, but I wasn't finding anything that contains Chicken in their "Bakery" page, until I found it under "Specialties". When I first read their menu I thought that the Specialties section were regular sandwhiches, but it turns out that they're dough baked in the bakery! Now this makes things MORE interesting. Im assuming it was the "Amigo's" specialty that I've tried and as mentioned it was amazing. Not only that, but there are many other specialties mentioned, and I have my eyes on the Roasto!

There seemed to be a shift in the clientele, and the music playing was considerably louder than our previous visits. To make matters worse, when we received the bill, it felt inflated, further diminishing our overall experience. We have been patrons of this establishment numerous times before, but after two consecutive disappointing visits, we have decided not to return. While the prices were already on the higher side, the unique experiences we used to enjoy made it worth it. Unfortunately, recent occurrences have led us to conclude that this is no longer the case. review_text: [4.5] [9 years ago on Zomato]: Can one be addicted to Hot Dogs and Nachos?? We would like to thank BRGR.CO management for receiving us along with a group of sweet foodies for a tasting session of some additions made on their new menu. It wasn’t our first time at BRGR.CO actually, the place is still gorgeous and very pleasantly decorated and their service remains unchanged: Superior is the best word to describe servicing in this “casual” American fast food We were served: • New York style salad: a “passe-par-tout” salad that should play to all tastes, • Golden chicken filets: Unlike most chicken strips, chicken tenders available over the Lebanese market, these chicken filet starters are very similar to escalope and are super tasty. They take very little frying oil and remain crispy. • Nachos: Among the BEST! Topped with double layers of Swiss and cheddar chesses and served with jalapeno, a succulent salsa, a very nice guacamole, and an outstanding sour cream. This nacho starter is really to DIE FOR. • Coney Island Dog: NEVER MISS THIS ONE. Rarely found over the Lebanese market, this pure American style hot dog is made of sausage topped with corn carne like ground meat sauce, yellow mustard and raw white onion cubes... add twenty times the word “very” followed by the word “delicious”. • Fish and chips: a good coating and frying for this sea bass filet.. The side fries were super tasty as well. • Fries and Cheese: all two thumbs up for this plate, one of our all-time favorite at BRGR.CO Now the burgers: • A Mushroom Swiss burger and a Portobello and Smokey Burger: Both delicious but leave it them to the end of your meal.  Portobello is a very light mushroom in terms of calories however very peculiar in terms of cooking and taste. One hint to be given here is NEVER to smell the mushroom or it will take a while before being able to taste anything else. We did it ourselves and we kept eating and all food ended up tasting and feeling the mushroom taste. • Truffled Provolone burger: The bestie in terms of acceptance by foodies and clients, an easy going one loaded with flavors, specifically provolone cheese. • A veggie Portobello mushroom burger: in one word; not for us. Portobello is very delicate when it comes to cooking and has loads of taste in every bite. The Portobello veggie burger proposed by BRGR.CO comprises of a full Portobello, like the whole mushroom! However, a smoother recipe might do the job like a combination of chopped Portobello, black beans, assorted herbs, very little garlic, would also deliver a hearty tasty goodness for veggie burgers lovers while reducing / hindering the strong taste of Portobello. Now the deserts: • Minnesotta Fudge: Mouthwatering from A to Z... A straight Recommendation for us • Caramel and date Pudding: Amazingly prepared with heavenly tastes if one is used to pudding! • White chocolate cheesecake: the least tasty among all three deserts but does the job if tasted alone or before the fudge and the pudding In sum, BRGR.CO ABC Ashrafieh, is a very plausible place for a causal High end American Fast food experience where one would enjoy tasty / addictive meals in a relaxed setting.

review_text: [5.0] [6 months ago on Google]: @burgerlayover Buco open its doors at the end of 2023 by chef Tarek who is ex-sous chef at Noma in Denmark. Their main courses are mostly burgers and they do have amazing starters for those who don’t feel like having burgers. We ordered the naked wagyu with hakkaido milk bun, 200gr wagyu meat and provolone cheese. The miso bbq with 200gr Australian grain-fed, mature cheddar cheese, jalapeños, pickled red cabbage & homemade miso BBQ sauce, Hokkaido milk bun. And Mulberry bacon with 200gr Australian grain-fed, pork bacon, cheddar cheese, crispy onion, mulberry jam, Dijon mustard, potato bun. They all served with very well fried french fries. Both the wagyu and the australian grain-fed meats were super fresh and juicy. My fav was the mulberry burger comes on a soft, shiny potato bun that gives a nice pillowy bite without overshadowing the fillings. The Australian grain-fed beef delivers a rich, meaty flavor, juicy and tender, which pairs well with the sharp cheddar melting into it. The crispy onion adds a satisfying crunch to break through the softness, while the pork bacon layers in a smoky, salty punch. What really makes this burger stand out, though, is the mulberry jam—sweet and slightly tart, it balances the richness of the meat and cheese beautifully, creating that sweet-salty contrast that keeps you going back for another bite. The Dijon mustard sneaks in just enough sharpness to cut through the sweetness and fat, tying everything together. Overall: this burger is indulgent yet balanced, with a clever twist from the jam. The bun holds well, the textures play nicely, and every bite hits salty, sweet, tangy, and crunchy notes. The fries on the side look golden and crisp, served stylishly in a martini glass—definitely adds to the presentation. Staff are great and loved the atmosphere. Service: Dine in Meal type: Dinner Food: 5 Service: 5 Atmosphere: 5

review_text: [4.0] [11 months ago on Google]: I make it a point to have lunch in Byblos at least once during every trip to Lebanon, and I always choose a restaurant overlooking the port. Byblos is my favorite spot in Lebanon, and I’ve noticed the souk has improved a lot over the years. During my most recent visit, we had lunch at Bab el Mina, where we got a table on the terrace with a direct view of the port, a definite highlight. We ordered fresh fish (both grilled and fried), along with some seafood dishes and traditional Lebanese mezze like hummus and salads. The fish was undeniably fresh, and everything tasted excellent. My only complaint is that the portion sizes for mezze seem to have decreased over time, maybe that’s a new trend in Lebanon. Overall, I had a wonderful experience. The owner personally welcomed us, and later stopped by our table to chat. The service was outstanding, better than many other places I’ve visited recently. I’d certainly recommend it and plan to return. We were a group of five and paid around 70 USD each, which I find reasonable for lunch with top-quality fish like Loukoz and Sultan Ibrahim. Additionally, they’ve opened new apartments for rent on a daily basis right above the restaurant. We took a quick look, and they appeared cozy and spotless. Service: Dine in Meal type: Lunch Food: 4 Service: 4 Atmosphere: 5 Recommended dishes: Fresh Fish, Fried Red Snapper, Fried Sultan Ibrahim, Calamari, Octopus Salad, Fattoush Salad, Fresh Seasonal Salad, Fish Grilled Fish

review_text: [5.0] [3 years ago on Google]: On my way to Jbeil, I was worried about the places that I would visit seeking food for all the places that I looked up on the internet web searches and social media are touristic places that only foreigners nowadays can afford. That is when I stopped searching and followed my gut that I would get lucky and find a few affordable places out there. After reaching Jbeil and exiting the bus, I walked down the stairs next to the road that would lead to the Old Souks. On my way down I stumbled upon a bakery called "Bake-In" and asked for the prices, surprisingly I was shocked for the prices were nothing compared to the ones I found online. I ordered a Keshek Manoushi for 40,000 L L and Half Cheese Half Thyme Manoushi for 35,000 L.L and the taste was incredible! The presntation was genuine and unique with the Manoushi served on wooden plates. The dough was thin and light on the stomach not disturbing at all. The taste of the Cheese was authentic and nothing like you could taste nowadays in most bakeries. The thyme as well was really good. When it comes to the Keshek Manoushi, the Keshek was great, finally real Keshek and not tomato and onion paste spread over the dough. One comment about the Keshek Manosuhi that I told the owner and he accepted it without any disturbance is that it needed a little more spread on it. Otherwise everything was great and it was the start of an adventurous day at Byblos, Jbeil.

review_text: [3.0] [4 months ago on Google]: We visited Bavaglino for lunch today and, unfortunately, the experience was significantly marred by the disorganization and lack of communication from the service team. review_text: [3.5] [10 years ago on Zomato]: Such a lovely place with interesting decor. We visited tonight and it seems business is slow. Only 3 tables were occupied and the sushi floor was deserted. We put our order and asked the waiter to get us some bread because we were really hungry. That took a while, yet when the bread arrived we were pleasantly surprised by it superior quality. The bread was served with an odd yogurt dip. The food slowly started arriving. The appetizer was the tricolor cake, grilled eggplant, halloumi cheese, sundried tomatoes, and pesto sauce. Not an original dish, however very well executed and well presented. I loved it. Australian tenderloin: served on the rock with grilled vegetables and pure a l'anciénne. The meat was heavenly. Very tender and succulent. And the fact that I grilled it myself meant that it was done to my preference exactly!! The 2 sides I selected were sadly very poor. The grilled vegetables (I expected asparagus, mushrooms, carrots, and cherry tomatoes on a vine) were a boring mixture of tasteless eggplants, zucchini, cherry tomatoes, and fennel. The mashed potatoes were too soupy and had baby food texture. Australian tenderloin: served with two different sides, spinach cream and potato wedges. Those two tasted much better than the other sides and also were served hot unlike the other two. BR cheese burger: divine in every way!!! Loved it. Pain perdu: also rich and comforting. Served with a cold caramel sauce. Unlike other places, no icecream. The place is worth a visit at the first weekend in ur month. It's not cheap and will cause a dent in your monthly budget. The quality of meat served explains the price. The menu needs tweaking as some of the sides were not as I expected them to be with such a price tag. Two bad things I noted were the very very slow (yet good) service and the poor ventilation. Our table and another table were eating off a rock and the odors filled the place, I don't want to be there when the place is at full capacity. Generally, I do recommend this place.

review_text: [3.0] [7 years ago on Zomato]: Visiting the Berdawni in Zahle during summer is a ritual to almost all the Lebanese people. So I went there with the family and we picked "Casino Arabi" to be our destination. We were well welcomed and guided to our reserved table. We chose to have the formula of 40$ per person. First, we were served a collection of cold and hot "Mezza". The portions were generous. The taste was in general very satisfying. The "Tabbouleh" and the "Fattouch" were prepared with fresh vegetables. The "Hommos" and the "Chanklich" were among our favorite items. The "Cheese Rolls", the "Kebbe" and the "Sambousik" were very appetizing and tasty. The raw meat was of high quality. The second part of the lunch was the mixed grills that were distinctively delicious, especially the grilled meat and tawouk chicken. The freshly baked "Markouk" bread was great. The last part was of course a big variety of fruits. Concerning the ambience, it could have been better if some traditional Lebanese songs were played. Finally, it's important to mention the poor service that we encountered, in hope of improvements. Although the waiters were kind, they showed slowness in their movements and in answering our requests. It was clear that there was a lack of organization and the waiting times between every change of platters on the table was significantly very long.

review_text: [5.0] [a year ago on Google]: Casino Mhanna is one of the best, if not the best, traditional Lebanese restaurants in the country. I usually go to their Dbayeh branch in Beirut, but their Zahle branch (their first and original branch) is picturesque and a must stop if you're in and around the Bekaa. They say the best way to judge a Lebanese restaurant is from their hommos, and Mhanna's doesn't disappoint, whether from it's freshness or the generosity of the portion. On a first visit, you shouldn't miss: baba ghanouj, grilled cheese rolls, fattoush, tabboule, chanklish, and mixed grills, and more importantly, the raw kebbe. Don't forget to leave some space for the fruits, and make sure to ask for the available desserts, especially the mafrouke and their ice cream. review_text: [2.0] [a year ago on Google]: I never had high expectations for the food at this place, but last night we found ourselves giving it a try. As predicted, it was a regrettable decision. I’m not usually a picky eater, but my experience there was bad to the point of me writing a review here. As a start, they used to have a grilled chicken burger on the menu, and now it’s gone and they barely have any options for the burgers, even after asking if they can do it (how hard could it be to put the grilled chicken in a bun instead of a baguette?). I ended up ordering the chicken sub, where the bread was dry (nay, even crunchy) and seemed not fresh, and the stuffing was on one side while the other was empty. Above all, I asked for iced tea, and they didn’t have any, so I ended up taking lemonade, which was average and the glass didn’t contain much of it for its price. The fries were not that good either and had an aftertaste of bad oil, so I asked for ketchup, and even that was not available (in a whole restaurant)! To top it all, I got what seemed to be a hair in my sandwich, and when I showed the waiters they dismissed it as rather a plastic string Well, why is a plastic string in my sandwich to begin with?! You seriously can’t depend simply on the ambience of your place while neglecting the rest of the factors, which perhaps are the reason the place wasn’t packed on a Saturday night, like it used to be. What truly sets this restaurant apart, beyond its stunning aesthetics, is the outstanding service. There's an abundance of attentive staff ensuring the quickest service possible. Our waiter was incredibly kind and helpful; they wouldn't even let us pour our own water or food! This level of dedication to service really makes you feel pampered. Now, let's talk about the food – it's simply delicious! The menu offers a wide and varied selection of authentic Lebanese and oriental dishes, catering to all tastes. I highly recommend trying the mushroom soup; it's absolutely divine and irresistible! To top it all off, after we finished our meal, we were delighted to be presented with complimentary desserts, ice cream, fresh fruit, tea, and coffee. I normally don't enjoy tea, but the cinnamon tea they served was particularly special and truly stood out! This generous gesture truly embodies the renowned hospitality and generosity of the people of Tripoli. Dar al Amar isn't just a restaurant; it's an experience that captures the heart of Lebanese warmth and culinary excellence. Highly recommended! review_text: [5.0] [a year ago on Google]: My initial review was a 1 star review, but for the sake of fairness I readjusted it to 5 stars after the restaurant reached out to me and invited me over to try the East Village experience again, which I believe was a very nice gesture and it was 180° different that my experience last time. I am convinced back then during my first visit was probably a bad time for the restaurant after discussing it with Hamza the floor manager. Because this time around they exceeded on all levels for service, level, taste, ambiance. I can't wait to go again! Thank you Hamza for making sure we experience the true east village experience. _____________________________ Disappointing Experience I came in with high expectations, but none were met. We wanted the onion soup, which a friend recommended, but it wasn’t available. Neither was the asparagus soup or the avocado salmon tartar—3 out of the 4 items we wanted. This was at 7 PM on a Sunday, which was surprising. The seating made things worse. A couple behind us was smoking indoors, and with no proper ventilation, it became unbearable. When I asked to move, I was placed by the entrance where cold air hit me every time the door opened. I had to wear my coat and scarf while eating, and no one seemed to care about my discomfort. I ended up packing my food and leaving early. Service was also disappointing. No one asked how the food was or why we were leaving so soon. I had to yell to get the waiter’s attention for the check. As I handed it over, I shared my disappointment, giving him a chance to address it, but he seemed indifferent, simply saying, “I’m just an employee; there’s nothing I can do.” That ended the conversation, and I left even more frustrated. To be fair, the risotto and guacamole were great, but the burger was just okay. I was hoping to come back and try the onion soup and salmon tartar when available, but after this experience, I don’t think I’ll ever return. For a bistro with this reputation, I expected so much better. Service: Dine in Meal type: Dinner Food: 5 Service: 5 Atmosphere: 5

review_text: [4.0] [9 years ago on Zomato]: Better late than never :-) I had the opportunity to try this place around a month ago thanks to the lovely and beautiful Zomato team (much love?) with some wonderful people. We kicked it off with an edamame salad, goat cheese salad, parma ham and melon, and salmon and tuna tartare. The 4 were pleasantly fresh and light. I loved how they incorporated fruits in the starters. Best of both worlds. Then came to amaaaazing risotto al limone which was seriously to die for. Definitely my favorite. The orrechiette ai gamberri that followed was alright, sorta lacked flavor but wasn't too bad i guess. Pretty average compared to everything else. The steak frites was also disappointing :-( The meat was annoyingly overcooked and turned cold like half a minute after i received my plate, and i didn't find the sauce on the side very interesting. Okay as for desserts, wow. I'm still not sure if i fell in love with the lavender creme brulée or absolutely hated it, but it was... something. They also look like tiny little galaxies in pretty white bowls and i think i must've stared at them for at least 4 minutes. The pavlova was really good as well as the macaron. Fondant was amazing. The staff were very friendly but unfortunately not always around. We also had the pleasure of meeting the chef and having him explain the concept of our lunch and the secret of the great lavender creme brulée :-) The place is very cute and colorful. Very happy. Very positive. Loved the ambience. Recommended!!

review_text: [4.5] [9 years ago on Zomato]: Ecafe Sursock, a beautifully refined french restaurant. Don't you just love it when you go to a restaurant and every meal is simply delicious. First of all, the portions were very generous. We started off with some salads, an edamame salad and a goat cheese salad followed by a proscuitti di parma con melone. It was my first time having parma ham with slices of melon, simply delicious, not to miss that beautiful presentation. Then came the fresh tuna and salmon tartar placed on a bed of avocado. The hot dishes included the risotto al limoni and pasta! The risotto was creamy and dense, filled with italian cheeses and a lemony taste. With regards to the main dish, I chose the Steak frites! One of my all time favorite dishes. A delicious piece of mouthwatering steak accompanied with pepper sauce and one of the best golden crispy fries I have ever had! When it comes to the deserts, my favorite was the fondant au chocolat.

review_text: [4.5] [9 years ago on Zomato]: éCafé bears nothing in common with a classic Parisian cafe. It's relaxed, inviting, and service-ready. Inside, plush sofas line the walls of the charming little bistro, which is divided into two dining areas. Comfy upholstered chairs, sufficient space between tables, and vibrant artwork affixed to the walls paint an inviting aura, one where you wouldn’t mind clocking in a couple hours or so. Make sure you try Chef Hicham Badran's seasonal edamame salad with citrus fruits and avocado. For mains, you really can't go wrong with any of their choices, though I am fond of the teriyaki-glazed salmon filet laying on a bed of carrot and zucchini ribbons. Dessert will, have you drooling, with an impeccable lavender creme brulee, pavlova crowned with a berry coulis, pistachio macaron sandwiching vanilla-raspberry swirl ice cream, and a decadent chocolate fondant with vanilla bean on the side. Come here for delicious food in a nice, warm ambiance with attentive service. Thanks to Zomato for the lovely lunch meetup.

review_text: [5.0] [6 years ago on Zomato]: Visited this place with a friend + a family of four (including two children). Two of us were non-Lebanese. It was dinner time and the place was packed. We sat indoors. Service: Very attentive and always available. There were many waiters around ready to help at any moment for anything we needed.  The waiters even intervened when we tried to serve our own food and offered to serve it for each one of us. The same applied to the wine. Waiters were good English speakers. Ambience: Pros: Although it was packed, the crowd was decent, included couples, families and groups of friends. Not noisy - we never felt it given that it had an outdoor seating and the doors were well open. Cons: There was shisha inside, but we never felt bothered. Food: Pros: Great variety (hot/cold  - veggies/meat) and freshly served (especially the bread). The fattoush salad had pomegranate which we thought was tasty. The sausages (Makanek) were warmly served in a small covered stainless pot.  Cons:  The menu lacked any Arabic translation. It was only in English. Price: Mid-high prices. Relatively expensive, but acceptable  given the value of the service and the quality of the food. For a table of 6 including two kids, we paid $285 The above shows that the waiters and staff have been carefully recruited (in quality and number), very well trained and properly paid and compensated. It reflected positively on their performance with the customers. The prices, although high, are understandable for a cafe in such an expensive land value Recommendations: Salads:  try the fattoush. Hot food: try the  grilled sausages and soujouk. Desserts: Make sure you try the cotton candy with ice cream.

review_text: [5.0] [7 years ago on Zomato]: The offerings of this place are heavenly! If you're having your doubts, get rid of them and ORDER NOW. I was browsing zomato and searching something to eat, came by this place. The name intrigued me, so I directly went onto the reviews page and took a look at the photos. As soon as I saw the bread that they make the fajita sandwhiches in, I pulled the trigger immediately and gave it a go. On the other hand, when I took a look at the menu and their prices, they were EXTREMELY pocket friendly comparing the portion and quality /taste provided! I ordered as a delivery. The phone operator was friendly and helpful. And the order came within the deadline which is 30 minutes and arrived hot as if served in person. I ordered the: -Chicken cheese fahita plate -Beef cheese fahita sandwhich. Im really glad I gave it a go. Both sandwhiches were breathtaking! --The chicken cheese fahita comes with chicken breast, lettuce, cheese, and tomato "sauce",in a very delicious and crisp tortilla bread. I quoted the word sauce because it wasnt your usual liquid sauce, it was actually little cut tomato pieces. Although I think the sandwhich would have been Much better if real sauce was added as well, like mayo or something (which I will add on my very next order), but it was very tasty on its own,and I have no complaints. Accompanied by the sandwhich were DELICIOUS home made style golden Crispy fries, a huge portion of it, plus a tasty side of coleslaw and some pickles on the side. And again, all of it was extremely delicious and fulfilling. Now going on to the beef fahita! I'VE NEVER eaten beef slices so SOFT so TENDER in a sandwhich before. Almost the same ingredients are found in the sandwhich except beef instead of chicken. I was so satisfied with the beef sandwhich! As every time when I order sandwhiches containing sliced beef, Im always having doubts and fears of the meat being hard and unchewable. But not in this Case Definitely! I also think that adding a specific sauce to the meat sandwhich other than the tomato "sauce" would also make it THE perfect sandwhich, like BBQ or steak sauce for example, but I still do not have any complaints for sure! Overall, this place is HEAVEN as mentioned, I will be having my daily lunches from here!

review_text: [5.0] [a year ago on Google]: In the restaurant business, where fortunes can rise and fall very quickly, I was curious to find out what the secret was to this restaurant's survival for over 100 years. I also heard that they used pure fava beans instead of chickpeas, and that they added a little garlic, so I went looking for them. The owner told me that they were founded in 1914, had moved from various addresses to their current location, and were now in their fourth generation, But they are not arrogant or overly proud, rather very polite and friendly. I suppose that's one of the reasons they've been so popular with the locals for so long. Falafel, made from fava beans, has a slightly bitter and classic taste and goes well with a chilli sauce. The vegetables are well prepared, the tomatoes are finely diced and the passili adds the flavour of a tabbouleh salad. The price of LBP 200,000 is quite reasonable considering the quality and the current inflation in Lebanon. The service at this family-run business is heartwarming, with many customers coming in for 10 minutes at a time while I was there. The open kitchen above the counter made the place feel relaxed and homely. There are a few chairs in front of the shop for eating in. There is also a small chair in front of the counter for customers to put their luggage on, which shows that they are attentive to their customers. It's a bit tucked away, so it's not easy to stumble upon this place while walking down the street. But I appreciate Google Maps for guiding me to this lovely restaurant. # Beirut # Lebanon Service: Dine in Meal type: Lunch Food: 5 Service: 5 Atmosphere: 5 Vegetarian options: Falafel Sandwich

review_text: [3.0] [11 months ago on Google]: Located in the heart of historic Byblos, **Feniqia** offers a dining experience with a prime view and a menu that leans into Lebanese and Mediterranean flavors. While the setting is undeniably charming—nestled in a tourist-heavy area with a lovely ambiance—our meal was a bit uneven, leaving us with mixed impressions. We started with an **assortment of appetizers**, which were mostly enjoyable. The **hummus** was smooth and well-seasoned, the **moutabbal** had a nice smoky depth, and the **fattoush** was fresh with a bright, tangy dressing. However, the **makanek (Lebanese sausages)** were disappointingly dry and lacked the usual burst of spiced flavor, while the **calamari** was overcooked, leaving it rubbery rather than tender-crisp. Service began attentively, with our waiter offering recommendations and promptly bringing drinks. But as the restaurant filled up, attention waned—dishes arrived at inconsistent intervals, and we had to flag down staff for refills. Things improved noticeably once the owner (or manager) stepped in, gently directing the team, which helped smooth out the experience. Given its location in a tourist hotspot, **Feniqia’s prices are on the higher side**, even for Lebanon’s dining scene. While the quality of some dishes justified the cost, others fell short of expectations for the price point. **The Verdict:** Feniqia has a beautiful setting and some standout dishes, but inconsistencies in food and service keep it from being a must-return spot. With a bit more attention to execution and staff coordination, it could easily elevate itself. For now, it’s a decent choice if you’re in Byblos and want a meal with a view—just order wisely. Service: Dine in Meal type: Dinner Food: 3 Service: 3 Atmosphere: 3

review_text: [4.5] [8 years ago on Zomato]: Pleasantly impressed with Gada by Maillon, although to confess, I didn't really order traditional Lebanese home-cooking. I was seduced by Mom's Burger and the Chicken Escalope, which equally proved to be generous, satisfying, and wholesome. The burger is everything nostalgia would conjure up from childhood: a fluffy, seeded bun; a slender beef patty; crunchy fries; and creamy coleslaw. It just melts in the mouth effortlessly. The breaded chicken filets were crusted with crushed kaak and tasted like a homemade affair. No oil, no grease, no horrid aftertaste. The side salads comprised fresh cucumbers, cherry tomatoes, and chopped romaine, with a cup of lemon-mustard dressing on the side. And the brownie is absolutely stupendous, though admittedly it closely resembles moelleux au chocolat -- but, hey, I'm not complaining! Adorable, sturdy packaging. Ample portions. Affordable prices. Nothing Gada by Maillon doesn't have going in its favor! Next time, I want to sample the cordon bleu and lasagna (bolognaise or spinach). Oh, and the shawarma djeij sounds ravishing, too :)

review_text: [4.0] [10 months ago on Google]: Tucked away in the lively streets of Bourj Hammoud, Resto Ghazar is a must-visit for anyone seeking an authentic taste of Armenian cuisine in Beirut. Whether you’re new to Armenian food or grew up with it, Resto Ghazar delivers a memorable dining experience that feels both nostalgic and exciting. The menu offers a rich selection of traditional Armenian dishes, prepared with care and consistency. The manti, tiny meat dumplings served with a yogurt-garlic sauce and topped with spices, is a standout dish that many regulars swear by. Another signature favorite is the cherry kebab – a sweet and savory combination that balances tart cherries with grilled meat in a surprisingly harmonious way. Vegetarians will find plenty to enjoy as well. The itch (Armenian bulgur salad) and cold stuffed eggplants are both flavorful and satisfying. The sujuk and cheese rolls, made with spicy Armenian sausage, are the perfect appetizer to share. And of course, no meal is complete without their lahm b3ajin, which are among the best in town – thin, crisp, and generously seasoned. The setting is modest but warm. With simple decor and a few tables inside and out, note that indoor smoking is allowed, which might be off-putting for some diners. Resto Ghazar may not be the most polished or modern restaurant in Beirut, but it embodies the spirit of Bourj Hammoud: rich in heritage, full of heart, and proud of its culinary roots. If you’re craving a hearty, authentic Armenian meal in a relaxed setting, this local gem won’t disappoint. Meal type: Dinner Food: 4 Service: 4 Atmosphere: 4 Recommended dishes: Hummus with Meat, Cherry Kebab Platter

review_text: [4.0] [10 years ago on Zomato]: Lebanese people love food and that is one of the main reasons we have so many restaurants with many creative concepts that have taken over the Middle East and the world. Hakini Lebneni is the new baby from the awesome people behind Najjar a Lebanese bistro serving progressive food with a unique touch. The place is located in Ashrafieh facing Byblos headquarters where previously Cafe Najjar was located. The menu has endless choices with very reasonable prices. Their concept is to prepare less fatty food by using spices to give flavors instead of frying food. •Our "coup de coeur" was the Hummus Dip Bouquet. It consisted of 3 mini platters: regular hummus, hummus with caviar and hummus with dried figs. We adored the twists they made since we never thought that caviar or dried figs would give an exceptional result when mixed with the hummus. •The Bulgur Balila made the perfect start to our lunch as it contained bulgur and chickpeas topped with a veggie garnish in a refreshing lemon sauce. The combination of bulgur and chickpeas was great and the vegetables added a touch of fresh crunchiness to the dish. •The Black Lentil Baklawa was amazing as it consisted of crispy baklava dough filled with black lentil salad in a lemon sauce. We liked the mixture between the textures and the refreshing taste of the lentil salad. They have the option to add salmon and surprisingly it went very well with the lentil. •we found the healthy version of Shawarma. The shawarma platter consisted of 2 chicken and 2 beef shawarma wraps. The wrap was filled with either succulent beef or chicken and grilled. The oils in the filling made the wrap crispy although it was baked and not fried. The meat was very well marinated. The wraps were finger licking good. They were served with tahini and spicy tomato dip. We would have preferred garlic over the tomato for the chicken shawarma wrap. •The Taouk Wrap is a must try. It was very light and tasty. It consisted of oven-baked tannour bread filled with barbecued chicken breast and grilled peppers. The chicken slices were juicy and perfectly marinated. We loved the flavors in the sandwich. It was served with pickles, fries and a special sauce (kerchup base). The fries were seasoned, crispy and not oily at all. We would have preferred a garlic sauce. For desserts we had the Cinnamon Apple Cheese Halawa. When we talk about the originality of Hakini Lebneni we mean mixing cinnamon and apple with the traditional Halewe Bjeben that we love, and replacing the ashta with sweet cheese. The result was exceptional as it felt more fresh and lighter. They respected the "low fat" concept even in the dessert. We loved the light yet flavorful food served at Hakini Lebneni. We wish them the success in their plan of opening branches worldwide to let foreigners taste exquisite Lebanese food. This is the image that we want others to have from Lebanon.

review_text: [5.0] [6 years ago on Zomato]: Ah yes! Hani’s is considered as one of Beirut’s hallmarks for those who seek Lebanese Home-made burgers. I have heard a lot about it surprisingly from people of an older generation born in the 60’s and 70’s. Apparently they have been there for a long time. So its about time I try it. I ordered the Hani’s Burger as an Extra meal or double meal for 14’000 LL. I did not yet know what I was in for, so I was like “what the Hell, why not?”. To my surprise I got two burgers, a lot of fries, a portion of coleslaw salad, a portion of Russian salad, and 3 large pickled cucumber. Now, before I start I would like to point out (especially to those who wrote bad reviews) that this place is famous for HOME-made Lebanese burgers. One should adopt a more objective approach while writing a review. Comparing their burgers to classical American burgers or commercial burgers is not a fair deal. I mean “Yes” commercial burgers taste better (classical American even Way better); and “Yes” Hani’s burger is comparatively average in taste and mediocre in flavor; but THIS IS how its supposed to be!!!! They are not expected to be fancy burgers, they are just supposed to be better than what you or your Mom makes in the kitchen. To me that’s EXACTLY what it was. It was better than what is usually served at home. The patties were “yes” thin and of the generic frozen type “but” they tasted alright.  The ingredients were freshly cooked and well assembled. The portions were big and satisfying. Whoever was complaining about the lack in taste could have added cheese or an egg to the burger. Yes! They give you the choice to PIMP your Home-cooked burger. Overall, objectively speaking, for a home-made style fresh burger and excellent fries, Hani’s would probably be my most recommended place to go. As for portions and affordability, it ranks as one of the best. And guess what, I am giving it a 5. The force is strong with these folks!

review_text: [4.0] [9 years ago on Zomato]: I was scrolling through Zomato and noticed this place somewhere deep down the list of restaurants within the area, and the photos honestly made me want to try it out. So my friend and I called and ordered a Quattro Formaggi pizza topped with pepperoni, alongside a box of potato wedges and another box of mozzarella sticks. Then the order arrives, within reasonable time, and the first thing I notice is the extraordinarily huge box of wedges we got. Getting great value for the price: check. So I went straight to the main treat, the pizza, and it honestly looked, smelled, and tasted delicious. The blend between sauce, cheese, etc... was subtle and perfect, and the crust was as thin as it should be. (I normally hate how unnecessarily thick the crust is in Lebanese pizza restaurants) So far, so good. Great value, delicious pizza. By then I'd have given it a 5, had the mozzarella sticks not been freezing cold. I understand it's the winter and they'll cool up a bit when it's 8° or less outside, but I'm talking super cold mozzarella sticks here. They didn't exactly feel fresh, which was a pity. But other than that, the wedges were good (although also not as hot as they should be), the pizza was great, the sauces that came with the starters were delicious, and the overall price was quite decent. (30,000 LL for a medium customized pizza, a huge box of wedges, and a box of mozzarella sticks)

review_text: [5.0] [2 years ago on Google]: Definitely a 5 stars experience! Joulia is a serene mountain retreat in the heart of the loudest city. This place, without exageration, will be on my "Back Home" itinerary every single visit. I'll start with the food, we ordered the owner's recommendation: - "boulettes aux cerises": Kebbé has the perfect thickness to make it a bit crunchy yet not dry at all. The cherry sauce brings in the punch you need for a starter. - "Joulia et ses copines": we had some "clochettes" filled with an Armenian spices based sauce, I never tasted something similar, it's a full-bodied buttery thing that I can't describe further, cause I didn't understand it (in a positive way). - "Salade Joulia": la simplicité de nos montagnes fait la beauté. - "Teblé": very fresh, mad2ou2a mazbout I only regret not ordering 2 plates instead of 1. - "Kebbé mamdoudé aux ognions & pignons": encore une fois, la simplicité! An authentic Kebbé dish, kept as simple as it is, with the amount of onions that you'd always wish your mom adds to Kebbé bl Saynié. My only take is that the Kebbé layer can be less thick, to keep the flufiness noticeable. - Sweets: I got a customized dessert (big shoutout to the friendly team), a simple Lebanese cake with cotton candy, roses, and sorbet on the side. BEST HOMEMADE CAKE EVER. (PS: I'm not a dessert person, yet I was impressed). I want to really thank the team there for their great service, because that also makes a big difference when you visit a place for the 1st time. The staff are super friendly, clean and professional. The owner is remarkably hospitable, he explained every dish attentively, and made sure we order the best combination to make our experience really special and worth it. For me, that differentiates Joulia from other trendy places: it's not a commercial restaurant! The ambiance is really nice, the place is not so big, and the decor is heart filling: granite tables, Teta's dentelles, flowers and blue windows. It's simply a gem! Last but not least, if I want to describe Joulia in one sentence: elevating the harsh rural traditional mountain food to the level of elegant fine dining! My only take is that the Kebbé layer can be less thick, to keep the flufiness noticeable. - Sweets: I got a customized dessert (big shoutout to the friendly team), a simple Lebanese cake with cotton candy, roses, and sorbet on the side. BEST HOMEMADE CAKE EVER. (PS: I'm not a dessert person, yet I was impressed). I want to really thank the team there for their great service, because that also makes a big difference when you visit a place for the 1st time. The staff are super friendly, clean and professional. The owner is remarkably hospitable, he explained every dish attentively, and made sure we order the best combination to make our experience really special and worth it. For me, that differentiates Joulia from other trendy places: it's not a commercial restaurant! The ambiance is really nice, the place is not so big, and the decor is heart filling: granite tables, Teta's dentelles, flowers and blue windows. It's simply a gem! Last but not least, if I want to describe Joulia in one sentence: elevating the harsh rural traditional mountain food to the level of elegant fine dining! It's time to write a review. Nestled in a prime location in Beirut next to main entrance of the American University. First of all the staff were an absolute delight—warm, attentive, and incredibly efficient. The service was remarkably fast without ever feeling rushed. Our orders arrived promptly, a testament to the dedicated team. And oh, the taste! Bliss House serves up some of the most delicious sandwiches I have ever had. It's clear that the kitchen takes immense pride in every dish they create. The Chocolate Mou is not just a dessert; it's an experience. The "Mou" was so rich, so velvety, and so intensely chocolatey and nutty that it was pure decadence. Each spoonful was a journey into a world of deep, luxurious flavor. It was a masterpiece of texture and taste even it's not a rocket science to do it —the kind of dessert you dream about long after you’ve finished it. Please don't mess the taste while counting calories . Just enjoy the moment. And then there was the Strawberry Ice Cream cup we had today. This was not your average ice cream. The flavor was a burst of strawberry goodness, tasting as if it were made from the freshest berries. The texture was incredibly smooth and creamy, a perfect contrast to the richness of the Chocolate Mou. Together, they formed a perfect finale to an already outstanding meal. Bliss House isn't just a restaurant; everyone in Beirut and beyond knows Bliss House in Bliss Street as THE DESTINATION for anyone seeking exceptional food and a truly unforgettable dining experience. I highly recommend it to anyone in Beirut—and be sure to save room for the Chocolate Mou. It's a non-negotiable part of the Bliss House journey. review_text: [5.0] [7 months ago on Google]: Emm Georges in Byblos is truly a hidden gem. It’s literally right by the beach, with an unlimited blue view that makes the whole experience unforgettable. What makes it even more special is that it’s a well-known local spot, mostly frequented by Byblos locals and Lebanese, but not something you easily find online when searching tourist recommendations. We actually discovered it thanks to a local taxi driver (LEB Taxi, also highly recommend Elie’s services) from Byblos who told us it’s the cleanest, tastiest, and best value for money — and he was absolutely right. The food was excellent and incredibly affordable compared to most places in Lebanon. We ordered grilled shrimp, batata harra (spicy potatoes with coriander and garlic), calamari provençal, plus a tajine and shrimp provençal to go. With two soft drinks, the whole meal was under $70 for five dishes — which is amazing for the quality and quantity. On top of that, they spoiled us with a generous complimentary dessert: a huge plate of fruits, biscuits with raha (rose water loukoum), and two coffees. Even though we were full, they insisted we enjoy it because, as they said, “it would make them happy” — such a beautiful gesture. The service was impeccable. Jaafar, one of the waiters, truly stood out. He was so attentive, kind, always smiling, and he went above and beyond. He even helped us prepare the shrimp by hand since they still had the shells and tails — something I’ve never seen a waiter do before. He’s honestly a hidden gem within the restaurant itself. This place ended up being a highlight of our Byblos trip, and we’re already planning to return next year. I’ve recommended it to my family and friends, and my parents loved it so much they went the following weekend. If you’re in Byblos and want an authentic, delicious, and affordable seafood experience with unbeatable views and warm hospitality, I can’t recommend Emm Georges enough. Food: 5 Service: 5 Atmosphere: 5

review_text: [5.0] [2 years ago on Google]: L'abeille D'or is commonly regarded throughout Lebanon as the home of Knefe. Yes, since it's conception, L'abeille D'or has become a household name in Lebanon's local sugar industry, almost serving as a foundation for this same industry. Upon entering L'abeille D'or's realm of sweets and delightful pleasures, you are instantly greeted with the saccharine scent of sugary delights. A scent so robust that it seemingly causes the Earth's rotation to halt instantaneously, enabling you with the powers of levitation. After selecting from the plethora of almost - diabetes infested treats, the lovely employees will escort you to aforementioned selection from where you may consume. Now, please continue reading for the official review. For months, two words echoed freely through the vast chambers of my mind. Two words that seemed fictitious upon combination. Two words that truly encapsulated fantasies, and two words that could create a hallucinogenic utopia upon consumption. For months, I was under the justified belief that these two words were merely an impoverished soul's figment of imagination. These two words? Croissant Knefe. Upon visualization of this Vincent Van-Gogh like masterpiece, gallons of drool divulged from my taste buds, and it's heavenly appearance forced me to ponder the accompanied sins after it's gradual depletion (by me eating it of course). I can safely state that dopamine had never before engulfed my nervous system at the rapidity of the first bite of knefe croissant had. However, and this is a big however, this was only after the first bite. The Croissant knefe was enormous, brobdingnagian, a mammoth, monstrous, and any adjective in between. For the incredibly affordable price of around 4-5$, you are definitely getting your money's worth, and much, much, much, more. With that being said, *sigh*, we return to "however". As the number of bites progress, it becomes exceedingly difficult to distinguish each component individually, or any component at all eventually. What I mean to say is, by the last bite, all you can truly taste is sugar. Obviously, sugar is sugar (so you can't really complain and you must be of extremely dim-witted to mess up sugar) and thus the knefe croissant is a 4 stars out of 5. Moreover, as a follow peer stated, the knefe croissant is an "experience". Food: 4 Service: 5 Atmosphere: 4

review_text: [5.0] [a year ago on Google]: Its called Sfiha Baalbakiyeh, a very well known food in Lebanon, and these guys know how to do it. Must try it. Make sure you order some yoghurt which is called Laban, its fresh and delicious. Sfiha Baalbakieh is a type of savory Lebanese pastry, originating from the city of Baalbek. It's a small, open-faced pastry made with dough topped with a spiced ground meat mixture, typically lamb or beef. The meat mixture is seasoned with onions, tomatoes, and a blend of spices like allspice, black pepper, and paprika. The sfiha are then baked until the dough is golden brown and the meat is cooked through. They are often served hot with lemon wedges and yogurt, allowing you to squeeze some lemon juice over the sfiha for an extra tangy flavor. Sfiha Baalbakieh is a popular street food and snack in Lebanon, and it's also enjoyed as a mezze (appetizer) at gatherings and celebrations. The unique flavor combination and the satisfying texture of the dough make it a beloved dish among locals and visitors alike. review_text: [4.0] [11 months ago on Google]: If you're looking for an authentic Lebanese breakfast experience in Beirut, **Lakkis Farm** is an absolute must-visit. Our morning meal here was nothing short of fantastic—a feast of fresh, flavorful dishes that showcased the best of traditional Lebanese cuisine. From the moment we sat down, we were greeted with warm hospitality and a table quickly filled with an abundance of dishes. The spread was a dream for any breakfast lover: creamy **labneh** drizzled with olive oil, rich and garlicky **foul**, and freshly baked **manakeesh** with za'atar and cheese. The **hummus in tahini sauce** was velvety smooth, with just the right balance of nutty tahini and lemon. The eggs were cooked to perfection—whether you prefer them fried or scrambled with herbs, they were delicious. The selection of **cheeses**—from tangy halloumi to soft akkawi—paired wonderfully with the assortment of **olives** and crisp, colorful vegetables: cucumbers, juicy tomatoes, fresh mint, and sharp onions. Every bite was a celebration of freshness and bold, comforting flavors. The setting at Lakkis Farm added to the charm—rustic yet cozy, with a welcoming vibe that made us feel right at home. The service was attentive and friendly, ensuring our tea and coffee cups were always full and that we had everything we needed. The only minor drawback was the lack of a **dedicated non-smoking section**. While the overall experience was outstanding, having a smoke-free area would make it even more enjoyable for those who prefer to dine without cigarette or argileh smoke, especially in the morning. That said, the food and atmosphere were so exceptional that we’ll definitely be back. Here’s hoping for a non-smoking option in the future—it would make Lakkis Farm absolutely perfect! Meal type: Breakfast Food: 5 Service: 5 Atmosphere: 2

review_text: [1.0] [a year ago on Google]: Extremely Disappointing Experience on Mother’s Day I am writing to express my profound disappointment with the experience we had at your restaurant today, particularly on such a significant occasion. We chose Liza to celebrate Mother’s Day, trusting that it would be the usual satisfying experience we’ve come to expect. Unfortunately, that was not the case. I made a reservation for lunch a week in advance, yet the hostess failed to inform me that a wedding was taking place at the same time. Upon our arrival, we were shocked to find ourselves seated in a very cramped area, squeezed between the welcome drink station and the wedding lunch. The noise from the wedding, including loud music and the chaos that came with it, made it impossible for us to enjoy our meal and properly celebrate the occasion. It is incredibly disappointing that you chose to accommodate 3-4 tables for extra profit, despite already hosting a wedding. Had I been informed about this situation when I made the reservation or when the hostess confirmed our booking on the same day, I would have reconsidered dining at Liza. Furthermore, I had a baby under one who was forced to endure the overwhelming noise. We struggled to hear each other over the loud music and were forced to shout to hold a conversation. The staff, meanwhile, were running around and shouting from the windows. When we asked one of the waiters to tone it down, his response was, “We are at a restaurant, not a nursery,” which I find to be completely unacceptable and disrespectful. I requested to speak with a manager to address these issues, but no one came to our table. This lack of response further highlights the lack of professionalism and attention to customer satisfaction at Liza we usually expect. As former regulars at Liza’s, I must say that this experience has left us deeply dissatisfied. Given the events of today, I cannot see us returning to your restaurant in the future. Unfortunately, what should have been a special celebration of Mother’s Day was marred by poor planning, inadequate communication, and a complete lack of respect for your customers. Tina Mansour Food: 3 Service: 2 Atmosphere: 1

review_text: [1.0] [a year ago on Google]: Loris used to be one of my favourite Lebanese restaurants, but after my last experience, I won’t be setting foot there again. I had called on Monday using the number listed on their Instagram to make a reservation for a business dinner. However, when my guests arrived, they were told there was no reservation. Not only was there no attempt to accommodate them professionally, but they were also spoken to rudely. When I arrived a few minutes later, the man at the door—who I assume was the manager—was just as unprofessional. Instead of handling the situation properly, he was dismissive and even accused me of lying in front of my guests. He also implied that he had no way of knowing which of his employees had taken the reservation and insisted on having the lady’s name—when she hadn’t given it to me on the phone. Rather than take responsibility for their mistake, they shifted the blame onto me. There were clearly available tables, yet we were made to wait without any apology. Unfortunately, the bad experience didn’t stop there. The service was extremely poor—two of the items we ordered were completely forgotten, and we had to remind the staff before they finally brought them. To make matters worse, the waiters seemed more interested in watching a card game at a nearby table than actually doing their job. Instead of ensuring a smooth dining experience, they were distracted, which likely explains why our order was mishandled. This was a business dinner, and it went wrong from start to finish due to their mismanagement and lack of professionalism. Loris has lost a loyal customer. It’s disappointing to see such a decline in service, and I wouldn’t recommend this place to anyone looking for a reliable dining experience. review_text: [5.0] [2 years ago on Google]: I had the pleasure of dining at Mc N Cheese Beirut recently, and it was an absolute treat for both my taste buds and my heart! From the moment I stepped inside, the warmth of the place, coupled with the attentive and friendly staff, made me feel right at home. The staff at Mc N Cheese Beirut deserves a special mention, especially Nada, the owner's wife, who welcomed us with a genuine smile and took the time to show us around. She exuded a sense of pride as she revealed that this charming eatery was a family business since 2016, and that personal touch was evident throughout the entire experience. Though Chef Carlos, the owner, was absent during our visit, his passion for food and culinary expertise shone brightly in every dish we tasted. The menu was a delightful blend of classic and creative twists on the beloved comfort food - macaroni and cheese. From traditional cheesy goodness to mouthwatering gourmet options, the choices were abundant. The cozy ambiance of Mc N Cheese Beirut added to the overall appeal. It was a perfect balance between modern and rustic, with quirky decor elements that added to the fun and laid-back atmosphere. Whether you're looking for a casual hangout spot with friends or a comfortable place to enjoy a hearty meal, this restaurant delivers on both fronts. Now, let's talk about the food - oh, the food! Each dish we ordered surpassed our expectations. The macaroni and cheese variations were bursting with flavor, and the portion sizes were more than generous. I appreciated how they accommodated various dietary preferences with options for vegetarians and meat lovers alike. One of the standout dishes was the "Truffle Mac," which elevated the classic dish to a whole new level with its rich, creamy truffle-infused cheese sauce. It was an absolute indulgence! The "Mexican Fiesta" macaroni and cheese was another winner, with its spicy kick and colorful toppings adding an exciting twist. Moreover, the service was prompt and attentive. The staff was happy to offer recommendations and make sure we had everything we needed to enjoy our dining experience to the fullest. My only small suggestion for improvement would be to offer a few more side options to complement the main dishes like some crackers or some bread /but this minor detail certainly didn't overshadow the delightful experience we had. In conclusion, Mc N Cheese Beirut is a hidden gem that delivers an unforgettable dining experience. From the heartwarming family connection to the deliciously cheesy creations, this restaurant has left a lasting impression on me. If you're a macaroni and cheese enthusiast like me or just someone looking for a cozy and welcoming spot to enjoy a delicious meal, Mc N Cheese Beirut is the place to be!

review_text: [4.0] [6 years ago on Zomato]: I visited this lovely addition to Restos St.Nicolas after reading mixed reviews. The menu looked interesting and tempting. A young gentleman, yawned as he welcomed us in. The setup is lovely and very simple. Our waiter took over and gave us the freedom to sit wherever we felt like. It was much better, yet there was hardly any truffle flavor in it. It was plain fries with way too much oregano (which I don’t get) and Parmesan cheese on top. Stay away. I’m not sure I’d go out of my way to visit Mariolino. I didn’t leave with any special experience during this visit. Although the crust was special and the toppings were unique, the whole experience was lacking in a way. If you happened to be at Restos St.nicolas and in the mood for pizza, then this fine pizzeria will definitely satisfy your cravings. Yet choose very carefully what to eat. Recommended

The dessert consists of crispy puffed rice topped with 3 scoops of vanilla ice cream then it’s covered with a milk Chocolate shell. They have designed the place a little bit after Black Seed Coffee shop to make it look like it is their original design. They have more indoor tables than outdoor. Prices are not cheap yet they are not overpriced. Average price per sandwich is around 15 $ which may not be affordable for every one but is definitely worth the price. It is served with wedges (more like curvy chips) and side sauce. Drinks are ordered by choice. Yet I have to mention that their delivery service is as good as dine in or take away! review_text: [5.0] [7 years ago on Zomato]: The memories I share with this place are endless. To whoever has never tried this place and is speculating whether to or not, I would say put that speculation aside, and come try it immediately! Thanks to anyone who read this!

review_text: [4.0] [7 years ago on Zomato]: Updated 14/03/2019 Rating: 3.5/5 Visited Nasayem first time yesterday. Cozy small place with a nice setting and cool ambiance. Comfortable indoor-only seatings. Service is excellent and saff are amazing - hats off to Ahmad who served us greatly. The manager and owner, Hussam, kept checking on us in order to make sure everything is going alright as it should be. We started with the beef quesadillas. Slightly disappointing as it was over filled with meat lacking both flavor and texture. The bread was not that of a quesadilla as well, but rather a simple usual wrap. Others might like it, though; a matter of preference. A guacamole dip would be a great addition anyway. We also had the cajun salad that was good, but could have definitely been better. Fresh veggies with fried chicken pops on the top and the honey mustard dressing was the best part of all as it served as a great flavor enhancer. The sizzling mix was a tasty main. It consisted of both shrimp and chicken with cheese and mashed potato on the side. Recommended. Similarly, the pizza burger - small portion is medium already - was cheesy beefy and tasted more like a homemade pizza. They also serve freshly-squeezed juices; we really enjoyed orange and carrot that were both great and served as a crisp refreshing healthy complement to our dinner. Portions are extremely generous and prices are very affordable. All in all, that was a fairly good experience. Surely will come back for more. Original review: Based on a single delivery experience. It's so bland and has almost no flavor despite that it's annoyingly oversaucy, as if the sauce needed to be simmered down a whole lot more. On the other hand, and to be fair and square, we really enjoyed the tacos. Golden crispy fried chicken with a bunch of vibrant fresh veggies (tomato, radish, onion and red cabbage) wrapped in a yummy fresh taco bread. Very generously filled. Coleslaw is good, skin-on fries aren't. Too oily and soggy. Delivery is moderately fast. Portions are generous and prices are very pocket-friendly. Decent packaging.

review_text: [4.5] [10 years ago on Zomato]: Almost two weeks ago, I was invited to try the new menu at Olivo’s, the restaurant located at the mezzanine level, in Radisson Blu Martinez, Ain El Mreisseh, Beirut. If you’re going out with your other half, friends or family, I highly recommend you to try Olivo’s restaurant. ENJOY!

review_text: [4.0] [8 years ago on Zomato]: Papaya is just a great place to grab a cocktail with a few friends; whether its to sit in the shop or grab them to go, their cocktails and ice cream are highly enjoyable. The colors and design of the shop are so bright and lively, and it gives off an appetizing look due to the fact that there is a big fridge all filled with mouthwatering fruits, all ready to be cut or squeezed and served in a cocktail for our own enjoyment. To the left of the fruits fridge is the ice cream fridge filled with flavors such as Oreo and Snickers; which are really delicious, and other typical flavors such as Mango and Pistachio, but even in their simplicity, they taste truly wonderful. On my most recent visit, I went in with three of my friends, and even though the weather is pretty cold, all four of us were craving ice cream and cocktails. Two of my friends ordered first and they each simply got three scoops of the typical chocolate and vanilla flavors on a cone and they highly enjoyed it. My other friend and I, however, wanted something a bit more special and unique, so my friend ordered the “Panama”, which basically contains pieces of banana, pineapple and mango all swimming in together inside mango juice. This cocktail also has two scoops of ice cream added in to it, in which my friend chose the Mango and Oreo ice cream scoops as his options, and then finally it is topped with whip cream. My friend adored this cocktail. My choice was kind of an original choice. I’ve had their Chocolat Mou and Fraise Mou before, and they taste amazing. This time, though, I asked for a concoction between the two. So I asked for a mix of the chocolat mou and fraise mou where half of the cup would be filled with strawberry and the other half with chocolate and they would be both mixed in with each other along with whip cream and chocolate sauce at the top and bottom of the cup. Mixing in these two in a medium cup together was more than satisfying for a die-hard ice cream fan like me. Overall, this place is truly wonderful with its cocktails and ice cream. It’s a very clean shop and the prices are more than fair. I always get out of Papaya satisfied and I’ll always keep on coming back whenever I have big cravings. Thanks go to who read all this.
