review_text: [4/5] [Oct 26, 2017 from Google]: Indigo was a last minute decision, but it was exactly what we needed at that moment. After a long marathon-like day, we were looking for a place to just relax. Situated at the top of the fancy Le Gray Hotel in Beirut, Indigo provided an outdoor seating area underneath the stars. Dim lights created a cozy and romantic atmosphere, granted they also resulted in the reduced quality of my photographs. The lower part of the view was obstructed by pretty flowers and vines, but the upper part of tall structures managed to make it up to this restaurant perched on the roof. The waiters guided us to our table, and when they were present, the service was great. They were attentive, polite, and very professional. However, at times it was a bit difficult to get a hold of them. My significant other ordered wine from the wine list, but I felt like having a cocktail, which they readily made available from the bar next door. I should add that the Strawberry Mojito was really good and refreshing. The waiter came to us with a bread basket in hand, from which we chose the olive and multi-cereal pieces of bread. They were soft and delicious, especially after they were smeared with the complementary rich butter. We ordered the Crispy Duck Salad and Ahi Poke as appetizers. The crispy duck salad was a pleasant surprise, the crunchy bits of the crispy duck were a perfect addition of texture to the salad. As for the ahi poke, it was very flavorful and the sauce complemented the tuna well. For mains, we ordered the Thai Baked Sea Bass in Banana Leaf and the Black Angus Tenderloin. The sea bass baked in the banana leaf was as moist as it could be; it was extremely tender. Unfortunately, the accompanying rice was forgotten until we reminded the kitchen. However, the waiter was quick to apologize and did end up bringing the rice to our table. Moving on to the steak, it was a good chunk of meat, but nothing outstanding. To satisfy our sweet tooth, we ordered the Valrhona Chocolate Fondant and the Namelaka, which consisted of chocolate mousse, hazelnut biscuit, and passion fruit ice cream. Needless to say that everything becomes better with chocolate, and these were two solid chocolate desserts. The warm chocolate inside the fondant was a great way to end the meal. In general, Indigo has good food, mostly great service, and an intimate setting, with nothing separating you from the sky above.

review_text: [5.0] [5 months ago on Google]: When I was in Lebanon back in May, my brother-in-law insisted that I try Fish Market Abou Mounir because he knows how much I love seafood – and wow, wow, wow, what an experience! This place is truly a hidden gem and easily one of the best seafood spots I’ve ever been to. The location itself is perfect – it’s set right on the beach, so while you’re enjoying your meal, you also get to take in the beautiful sea view and fresh breeze. It creates the perfect Lebanese coastal atmosphere that immediately makes you feel relaxed and connected to the sea. The customer service was excellent from start to finish. The staff were warm, attentive, and very knowledgeable about their menu. They helped us choose from the wide selection of fresh fish displayed right in front of us. Everything is caught and prepared fresh, and you can tell the difference in every bite. Before diving into the seafood, we started with their Lebanese meza, and it was an absolute feast. We had hummus, tabbouli, fattoush, garlic potatoes, and a variety of small dishes that were bursting with flavor. Each dish was made with fresh ingredients and tasted exactly how traditional Lebanese meza should – light, vibrant, and full of flavor. Then came the seafood, and this is where Abou Mounir truly shines. We tried three or four different kinds of fresh fish, perfectly grilled and seasoned, along with calamari that was crispy, tender, and delicious. And the star of the table for me was the octopus – wow oh wow! It was grilled to perfection, tender yet smoky, and honestly one of the best I’ve ever had. What made the experience even more special was the way it ended. After the feast, they served us cookies along with Turkish delight – something we used to enjoy growing up in Lebanon. That small touch brought back so many wonderful memories and made the whole meal feel even more authentic and heartwarming. We basically tried a little of everything, and not a single dish disappointed. The portions were generous, the quality was top-notch, and the entire experience felt like a true Lebanese seafood celebration. If you’re in Lebanon and you love seafood, you cannot miss Fish Market Abou Mounir. Between the unbeatable beachfront location, the fresh catch of the day, the delicious Lebanese meza, and the warm hospitality, this place has it all. I left completely impressed and can’t wait to return on my next trip. Highly, highly recommended! Food: 5 Service: 5 Atmosphere: 5

review_text: [5.0] [2 years ago on Google]: Rajasthani cuisine is the cuisine of the Rajasthan region in North West India. It was influenced by various factors like the warlike lifestyles of its inhabitants, the availability of ingredients in an arid region and by Hindu temple traditions of sampradayas like Pushtimarg and Ramanandi.[1][2] Food that could last for several days and could be eaten without heating was preferred. Scarcity of water and fresh green vegetables have all had their effect on the cooking. Signature Rajasthani dishes include Dal Baati Churma, Panchratna Dal, Papad ro Saag, Ker Sangri,[3] Gatte ro Saag. It is also known for its snacks like Bikaneri bhujia, Mirchi bada and Kanda kachauri. Other famous dishes include Dal Baati, malaidar special lassi (lassi) and Lashun ki chutney (hot garlic paste), Mawa lassi from Jodhpur, Alwar ka mawa, Malpauas from Pushkar and rasgulla from Bikaner, "paniya"and "gheriya" from Mewar.[2] Originating for the Marwar region of the state is the concept Marwari Bhojnalaya, or vegetarian restaurants, today found in many parts of India, which offer vegetarian food of the Marwari people. The history also has its effect on the diet as the Rajputs preferred majorly a non-vegetarian diet while the Brahmin, Jains, and others preferred a vegetarian diet. So, the state has a myriad of both types of delicacies.[4] ￼Royal Rajasthani Thali served at Rambagh Palace, Jaipur According to a 2014 survey released by the registrar general of India, Rajasthan has 74.9% vegetarians, which makes it the most vegetarian state in India.[5]

review_text: [3.0] [a year ago on Google]: We recently had breakfast at Abu Hassan Hummus and Fool in the Alhamra branch, Beirut. We ordered the fool and fatet tahinia. The ambiance of the place was welcoming and the staff were friendly and efficient, which started our meal off on a good note. The service was impressively fast, and they were attentive to our needs throughout our visit. One notable aspect was the generous complimentary offerings: a variety of fresh vegetables and an ample supply of bread, which were much appreciated. These small touches added value to our meal and showed their commitment to customer satisfaction. However, we were slightly disappointed with the food itself. Both the fool and the fatet tahinia were served a bit cold, which took away from the enjoyment of the dishes. The flavors were decent but not outstanding, and given the reputation of Abu Hassan, we had higher expectations. For the price they charge, we anticipated a higher quality meal. Overall, while the service and extras were commendable, the main dishes left something to be desired. It's a decent spot for a quick breakfast with efficient service, but there's room for improvement, especially in ensuring the food is served at the right temperature and enhancing the overall flavor profile. review_text: [4.0] [4 months ago on Google]: After several takeaways and dine-ins, I can honestly recommend this spot for a quick, tasty meal on the go. The chicken shawarma is tender, juicy, and has that perfect lemony-peppery balance that keeps you coming back. The beef shawarma is good too, though I personally lean toward the chicken — it’s just packed with flavor. The garlic paste hits a nice middle ground — smooth, light, and not overpowering. They also have their own special house sauce, which is interesting and worth trying, even if it’s not exactly my go-to flavor. If you’re into burgers, try their crispy chicken burger — it’s that Lebanese-style crispy burger we all love, golden-fried and crunchy with a hit of garlic. The broasted chicken platter is okay, but the breading reminds me a bit of Lebanese kaak, which isn’t quite my style for broasted — still, not bad overall. Service is quick, staff are friendly, and prices are very affordable. The place is usually lively, with outdoor seating that’s great for a casual bite with friends or a quick solo meal. Definitely one of those reliable Dekweneh spots to grab a shawarma fix or crispy bite anytime. Food: 4 Service: 5 Atmosphere: 4

review_text: [3.5] [9 years ago on Zomato]: I've never sat and eaten at Al Walid, but I've ordered enough from them to know a thing or two about their fatteh bel laban and their hummus. First off, here's the thing about fatteh: there are so many variations of it. It's very uncommon to go to a place, try the fatteh, and find another place that has a fatteh that's similar to it. Some people do it with tahini, others with yogurt, others still with chicken, and some even do it with rice, and the ingredients and spices used are never quite the same. Some people even boil the yogurt. What the hell? So how would you describe fatteh to any person who's never had it? My answer would be: you show them the one served at Al Walid. Sure, there are better places to pick, but I can't tell you how many times I've ordered a fatteh at a big name restaurant and got served a bubbling abomination. People really seem to enjoy with this classic traditional dish for some reason. So back to Al Walid: their formula for the fatteh is tried and true. For one thing, you could clearly see the layers of fried bread, chick peas, yogurt, and fried cashews all neatly stacked on top of each other. For another, the amounts of each ingredient are just right; you'll never have to grab a fishing net to get the chick peas out of the bowl, and you'll never need to add extra yogurt to unbind the chick peas from the bread. And the garlic, a key ingredient that people usually get wrong, is ever so subtly present, with a shy yet inviting aroma. To top it all off, the portion's generous enough to satisfy anyone with less than four stomachs. It's not uncommon to see two persons splitting a bowl in half between themselves. I'll admit that I'm slightly less fond of their hummus, if only because there's nothing too special about it. Like the fatteh, it's more along the lines of tried and true, except here it's just one big bowl of plain hummus, so there aren't as many flavours involved. The upside is that you do get a 'service' with which you can liven up the taste of the hummus and make it an enjoyable meal on its own. On that note, I must say that it's a real shame that there are still restaurants out there that choose not to give service with something as simple as hummus! Nevertheless, Al Walid does have some problems. First, consistency: one look at the photos section and you'll know why. While the portion size is always fixed, on some days you might get less meat and cashews than normal, which is very annoying, considering that you're paying more money to have those in. Now, don't get me wrong, the prices are very palatable and actually rather cheap compared to other inferior joints, but when I ask for meat, I'd rather have its physical presence instead of only its smell, you know? And next week, everything's fine again... but maybe not the week after! The second problem Al Walid has is with the service. The tomato slices have never looked appetizing to me, but the mint can be especially troublesome. I like to chew some mint after meals like this, but sometimes I get a tuft of dusty, dirty mint leaves that crack and grind against my teeth and it just leaves me upset. Would I recommend the place? Sure, go ahead and try the fatteh, but don't forget to be specific with your order to ensure that you don't get some unpleasant surprises. Also, a tip: ask them to pack the fried bread separately.

review_text: [1.0] [7 months ago on Google]: Terrible Service and Disrespectful Treatment – Not Worth the Hype We recently booked a high table at Antika for a group of 4 & the experience was disappointing from the very beginning. We were told the minimum charge was $55 per person. However, when we arrived, they had booked us for 5 people and seated us at a table clearly meant for 4. When we requested to be moved to a proper table, we were told it wasn't possible—even though we could see empty tables and we were then told we'd have to pay extra to move, despite the fact that the tables were at the same section and cost. We asked for the manager several times. He never came. Strangely, when another table (four women) requested him, he appeared almost instantly and changed their table with no issue. When we raised this with him, he still refused to move us. Only after a lengthy and frustrating discussion did they finally switch our table. Service didn’t improve. No one came to pour drinks, we asked multiple times for an ashtray and were eventually given a small bowl instead. Our plates were cracked, we had to keep asking for basic things like straws, and overall the staff seemed indifferent at best. The final bill was outrageous—charged for 5 people instead of 4, totaling $409 which was above the minimum charge (although we expected to go above the $220 but not $409), they also tacked on an unexplained $15 per person "entertainment charge" which was never mentioned beforehand. When questioned, the waiter brushed it off saying, “It’s a small amount, not a big deal.” To top it all off, we brought a birthday cake and explicitly asked them not to cut it. Yet by the end of the night, they returned it to us half gone and it wasn’t even served at the table. This place left a very bad impression, and the only reason we always go there and if we ever think of going back again would be for the amazing Karim Nour, although we would prefer to go see him singing at another place Food: 3 Service: 1 Atmosphere: 4

review_text: [5.0] [7 months ago on Google]: While I was in Beirut doing some shopping for the family, I started to feel hungry and decided to try a place I hadn’t been to before—Arouset Labneh. I’m so glad I did because it turned out to be an excellent choice. It was me, my brother, and two of our friends. I had my eye on the beef shawarma, while my brother went for the chicken shawarma. Our friends decided to skip the platters and try the sandwiches instead. From the moment we walked in, the service stood out. Our server—whose name I sadly forgot—was friendly, attentive, and made us feel welcome from the start. One thing I really appreciated was the presentation. The shawarma platters were served on wooden trays, giving the meal a rustic, stylish touch. Everything was neatly arranged, and you could tell they put effort into making the food look as good as it tasted. The beef shawarma was flavorful, tender, and perfectly seasoned, with just the right amount of spices to give it that authentic Lebanese taste. The chicken shawarma was equally delicious—juicy, well-marinated, and paired perfectly with the sauces and sides. But it’s not just shawarma that Arouset Labneh does well—their kabobs are outstanding. Both the beef and lamb kabobs were juicy, tender, and packed with flavor. The fact that everything here is made to order makes a huge difference in taste and freshness. You can really tell the meat is grilled fresh for each customer, giving it that perfect smoky aroma and tenderness. The atmosphere of the restaurant added to the experience—it had a clean, modern feel but still carried a warm and inviting vibe. Combined with the great service, it made for a relaxing and enjoyable meal. Overall, Arouset Labneh was a fantastic find. Between the delicious shawarma, mouthwatering kabobs, beautiful presentation, and excellent service, it’s the kind of place I’d happily return to the next time I’m in Beirut. Whether you’re in the mood for a full platter or just a quick sandwich, you’re going to leave satisfied. Rating: – Great taste, great service, and everything made fresh to order. Food: 5 Service: 5 Atmosphere: 5

review_text: [3.0] [7 months ago on Google]: On my first visit, the experience was a mix of positives and areas for improvement. Parking & Entrance: Parking was very limited, and the entrance felt crowded with valet staff and hostesses, which made the arrival a bit chaotic and I had to park far and walk a couple of blocks. I was surprised when the hostess asked if I wanted to dine in, takeaway, smoking, or even an argeile—it was confusing since I thought this was a fast-food concept. Service: The server who took my order was polite. When I asked about the waiting time, she said 30 minutes, which felt long for “fast food.” However, to my pleasant surprise, my meal was served in under five minutes. Food: I ordered the broasted chicken. The portion looked fine, and the taste was decent though slightly too salty. The coleslaw (malfouf) was excellent—probably one of the best I’ve tried locally after KFC. Unfortunately, the bun that came with the meal was stale and fell apart, which was disappointing. review_text: [1.0] [8 months ago on Google]: Very Disappointed with Misleading and Inflexible Service We recently booked at BDP Lebanon for a group of 8 and specifically requested poolside seating in advance. Upon arrival today, we were told by the front desk lady that the poolside was “fully booked.” Out of trust, we accepted an alternative table by the beach. However, while heading to the WC and passing by the pool, I noticed that over 20 poolside seats were mostly empty with only 4 guests seated. I immediately asked to speak with the person in charge. The first explanation given was: “We cannot seat groups of 8 at the pool.” I offered a simple solution: we can be split as 2 groups or 4 couples—it’s still the same total of 8 seats and we’re fine with separate or single billing. Still, they declined. Then, a second excuse was presented: “There is a minimum charge at the pool.” This was never communicated to us at the time of booking. I made it clear that if such a policy existed, we should have been informed in advance so we could make a proper decision. No one mentioned this when we called to reserve. When we returned to our beachside seating, another staff member approached us with the same inconsistent reasoning, then added something even more surprising: “The minimum charge is up to me, and I can apply it at any time before, during, or after service.” Frankly, this was unprofessional, unclear, and completely arbitrary. We’ve visited BDP many times before and always made it a point to arrive early to choose good seating before the place gets busy. This time, even with plenty of empty poolside seating and a confirmed request, we were refused without any valid justification. No solution was provided. Just excuse after excuse. We were left very disappointed with how poorly this was handled. We hope the management takes this feedback seriously. Returning customers deserve transparency, consistency, and fair treatment.

review_text: [2.0] [11 months ago on Google]: Allegedly one of the fifty best restaurants in the Middle East, but I can think of fifteen better ones in Beirut alone. It's shockingly overpriced for the amount of food they give you. They advertise their menu as being a collection of shareable plates. And then, for a table of four, they give you a squid ink risotto with three prawns on top, leaving you in the ridiculous situation of having to divide three prawns between four people. For $30, you absolutely should not have to do that. Other dishes are similarly stingy - we were left asking each other "did you have enough?". They give you bread and muhammara for the table, but of course only two bread rolls between four. Good restaurants give you the impression of being hospital - as though the chef enjoys feeding people. Here, it feels like the kitchen is passive-aggressively trying to send you as little food as possible in the hope that you'll cave in and order more. The quality of the food is generally quite high. But there are so many better options in this city that don't give you the strong impression that they're trying to give you the absolute minimum possible in exchange for the price they're asking. Service: Dine in Meal type: Dinner Food: 2 Service: 4 Atmosphere: 2

It’s served with fresh vegetables on the side. Regarding the prices, they are every fair. The service is inconsistent. It’s also slow and sometimes you have to remind the staff several times of your order.

review_text: [5.0] [11 months ago on Google]: For decades, The Chase was more than just a restaurant—it was a cultural landmark, a meeting place for Lebanon’s greatest minds, and a home to countless memories. Since its opening in 1977 by Rachid Jreissati and Patsy Nader, it became a refuge for intellectuals, philosophers, artists, and journalists, a place where ideas flowed as freely as the wine. Opened in the midst of the Civil War, The Chase stood resilient through destruction, reconstruction, and reinvention, all while witnessing a Lebanon slowly fracturing. Located in Place de Bachir, it became the beating heart of Achrafieh, embodying the quiet resistance of its people. Political figures, philosophers, Achrafieh families, and Sunday wanderers all made it the intellectual and social hub of the capital. For many, it wasn’t just a place to dine—it was a symbol of endurance and culture. Despite its legacy, The Chase struggled in its later years, weighed down by economic crises, the pandemic, and Lebanon’s ongoing hardships. After finally closing its doors some five years ago, many feared it would remain just a memory. But now, with a complete makeover and new management, The Chase has reopened as The Chase Trattoria, helmed by Kamil Bouloot and Chef Charles Azar. Blending a fresh identity with the echoes of its past, the newly baptized trattoria retains some of its beloved dishes while embracing a renewed culinary vision. An excellent menu highlighted by succulent dishes and a courteous staff make the revamped The Chase a must-visit destination. Seeing it vibrant again, filled with people and conversation, feels like a breath of fresh air—a hopeful sign of a new era. Let’s hope so. Food: 5 Service: 5 Atmosphere: 5

review_text: [4.0] [7 years ago on Zomato]: I LOVE Karaoke even though I own the distinction of having perhaps the worst, most nasally voice in the entire middle east region. But, does that deter me from singing my guts out anytime I get the chance to? Nope! Drink N Sing Monot is my favorite Karaoke destination (especially after my previous favorite destination, Hard Rock Cafe, went out of business). We have rented the large private room twice so far and both times were a blast. Even though they don't serve food, we were allowed to order delivery and they provided the drinks, the hookah, and the salty snacks. Their song collection is large and encompasses all tastes, although it needs a little updating because the newer songs are hard to find [I wanted to do Cardi but couldn't find anything by her :( ]. But yeah I highly advise anyone who likes Karaoke to try renting a room at least once because it's really and therapeutic lmao. I always end up losing my voice for a few days after though haha.

review_text: [3.0] [11 months ago on Google]: Dupain – A Stylish New Spot in Saifi Village Tucked into the charming streets of Saifi Village, Dupain is a welcome addition to Beirut’s café and bakery scene. That level of attentiveness is refreshing and deserves to be acknowledged. Atmosphere: Where Dupain truly shines is its setting. The outdoor terrace, in particular, is a delightful spot to enjoy a quiet moment with coffee or a pastry, while watching the life of Saifi Village pass by. The Bread: A real standout. Whether or not you’re dining in, be sure to take home a loaf of their baguette or sourdough. The quality and flavor are exceptional, and a testament to the care put into their bakery side. Verdict: Dupain is a charming place to enjoy breakfast, coffee, or a sweet treat in a beautiful Beirut setting. While the service could benefit from more consistency, the professionalism of the management, the quality of the bread, and the relaxed atmosphere make it a spot worth returning to. Food: 4 Service: 3

Between the friendly service, excellent flavors, and variety of dishes, this is the kind of place you’ll want to return to over and over. review_text: [5.0] [7 months ago on Google]: During my recent trip to Beirut, I made a stop at Farouj Al Shams, and I can honestly say it was one of the most memorable food experiences I’ve had in Lebanon. This place is legendary for a reason. From the moment you arrive, you’re greeted by an incredible buzz—tables full of happy diners, the aroma of freshly grilled meats in the air, and an army of staff working seamlessly to serve everyone. Despite how crazy busy it was, the service was quick, professional, and genuinely warm. You can tell they’ve mastered the art of keeping customers happy, no matter how packed it gets. We decided to go all out and try almost everything on the menu. The broasted chicken was perfectly crispy on the outside, tender and juicy inside, seasoned just right so you could taste the flavors without it being too salty or greasy. Their charcoal BBQ had that authentic smoky flavor you can only get from a proper grill—each bite packed with the taste of Lebanese spices and slow cooking. The tabbouleh was fresh and vibrant, bursting with parsley, tomato, and lemony zing. The hummus was creamy and smooth, balanced with the right amount of tahini, while the baba ghanouj had that irresistible smoky undertone. We also enjoyed waraq 3inab (stuffed grape leaves) that were delicate and tangy, sujouk sandwiches filled with spiced sausage that had the perfect kick, and their fries, which were so addictive we ordered more even though we were already full. As if that wasn’t enough, the staff insisted we try their beef shawarma, carved fresh and loaded with flavor—it was tender, juicy, and easily one of the best I’ve tasted. The restaurant itself is huge, with plenty of seating both indoors and outdoors, making it great for groups or families. For those who don’t want to wait, they even have a large grab-and-go section with ready-made meals that still look just as tempting as what’s served at the tables. Everything we had was freshly prepared, made with quality ingredients, and served hot. What really makes Farouj Al Shams stand out is the combination of amazing food, vibrant atmosphere, and outstanding service. It’s more than just a restaurant—it’s a full-on Lebanese dining experience. If you’re in Beirut, this place is a must-visit, whether you’re looking for a quick bite on the go or a big feast with friends and family. Food: 5 Service: 5 Atmosphere: 5

Their responses were vague, suggesting either a lack of knowledge or a lack of willingness to engage with customers. Finally, the food (a saj) was a bit moist and ultimately unsatisfying. The presentation was also lackluster. Overall, Kalei Coffee Shop has potential with its rooftop location. review_text: [2.0] [2 years ago on Google]: I recently visited the restaurant within Kintsugi in Beirut, enticed by its promising fusion of style and gastronomy (or at least what they show on Instagram). The first impression was impressive—the interior design seamlessly blends modern aesthetics with a touch of cultural finesse. The professional staff, guided by a commendable floor manager, contributed to a welcoming atmosphere. The Negroni and Aperol Spritz were solid, setting the stage for an evening that, unfortunately, took an unexpected turn. Our dinner began optimistically with a roasted cauliflower—a dish that, despite its simple yet vibrant appearance, fell short in flavor, lacking the expected harmony of ingredients. The quinoa chicken salad and pasta al limone followed suit, arriving unfinished and lacking the promised zest. Regrettably, the low point was reached with the rancid chicken. This unfortunate choice left an unpleasant taste, overshadowing the positives of the evening. The saving grace was the swift action taken by the floor manager, who not only apologized sincerely but also promptly removed the subpar dishes from the bill. The inconsistency of the dishes is evident—the pasta's unmet potential, the quinoa salad's blandness, and the inexcusable state of the chicken. While the exterior and interior of Kintsugi sparkle with its branding and ambiance, it leaves much to be desired in the realm of culinary expertise. In conclusion, Kintsugi has the potential to be an urban haven for travelers and residents alike, but it needs a considerable overhaul in its F&B offerings. It's a picturesque shell with a promise yet to be fulfilled, leaving diners like myself and my friend yearning for an experience that matches the allure of its aesthetic facade. Service: 3 Location: 3 Hotel highlights: Quiet

review_text: [4.0] [7 years ago on Zomato]: We got stuck in so much traffic on our way to have breakfast at L’Atelier du Miel but it was worth it. The staff was very friendly and we were welcomed with a taste of just-made chocolate confections. What I liked about L’Atelier du Miel was the pride and passion that seemed to exude from their products. This was shown in the knowledge of how their honey is made, as well as in the various types of honey featured in the items on their food menu. I appreciated that the paper placemat had the map of Lebanon on it, with a colored legend telling us which honey was made where. I also loved that my hot chocolate was infused with honey and that their strawberry jam was deliciously sweetened with the golden syrup. While my other half indulged in poached eggs with smoked salmon (one of the things on my list to eat as soon as I give birth), I had the scrambled eggs. They were so fluffy and creamy sitting on a slice of bread, and I really enjoyed them. I added some of the olive tapenade that came with the bread basket to them as well. The olive paste was great and nothing beats freshly baked bread. As for the croissants…yummy! They were so crispy and flaky. The stack of pancakes was my least favorite item; I did not feel that they were as fluffy as they should be. They were generously engulfed with honey, which rendered them a tad too sweet. However, to be fair, I was the one that had to order them without the accompanying berries, which I am sure would have added the necessary tartness that would balance the flavors. At the end of the breakfast, I was surprised with a lovely gesture: a box of Nougats as a gift for the constantly hungry baby kicking in my womb. We also could not leave the premises before taking some of their honey home with us. The comfortable ambiance at L’Atelier du Miel made me feel good on the inside, and I will be returning to taste their salads, sandwiches, and hot platters—of course, adorned with honey.

review_text: [4.5] [8 years ago on Zomato]: A hidden gem all about honey between the vintage buildings in Mar Mikhael!! I fell in love with everything in this place! From the atmosphere, to the decor, to the service, and most importantly the remarkable food experience!!!!! Atmosphere and decor: Located between the old buildings of Mar Mikhael, the place full of greenery is very calm, ans soft music is played in the background. You can find a collection of magazines and cookbooks all talking about honey. Once you enter the place, you will feel this mystical charm like no other place in Beirut. Service: The waiter was really helpful and very professional, and our order was on time. It was really delightful too that the owner came over and asked us about the new creations they are working on. Food experience: First, I really like the menu presentation, that for each dish a specific type of local honey produced by the place itself is recommended. You can find very interesting types of honey combining local flavours such as thyme, orange blossom... We ordered two desserts dishes: the crispy homemade waffles and the chocolate ashta cream, and both are beautifully presented. The waffles were nicely done, crunchy yet smooth, topped with fresh avocado amd strawberries, dressed with sweet honey and garnished with colourful flowers. The chocolate ashta cream was a heavenly good combination of chocolate mousse, fresh ashta, dark chocolate bits, crunchy meringue drops, all laying on a moist brioche base. And all of this is topped with a sweet tangy carobe honey. The contrast in textures was phenomenal; you get the smoothness of mouse and ashta, the crunchiness of biscuits and meringue drops, and the remarkable taste of carobe honey. Then we had the chance of trying the new creations of the house: sugar free nougats and gingerbread. It was a very exceptional experience, in an enchanting place that should not be missed.

review_text: [1.5] [8 years ago on Zomato]: Possibly the strangest restaurant experience I've ever had. I was pressured to order and when I asked for recommendations, the menu items and their descriptions were just read back to me which wasn't very helpful. I had read over and over again about people receiving honey plates with four different honeys, we weren't offered such thing. review_text: [3.0] [9 months ago on Google]: L’Entrecote de Paris au Pirate, recently opened in the heart of Saifi Beirut. We really had high expectations and were excited to try it, but sadly ended up disappointed on several issues. This restaurant has no link to the real official french chain Le Relais de l’Entrecote, which has a branch not far away in Beirut. We heard that the owner worked at an Entrecote in Paris, and opened his own version in Lebanon. Why not? We wish him all the best on that. We had a reservation, walked in and there was no one to greet us and take us to our table. We had to wait a bit standing in the middle of the restaurant, for someone to finally notice us and take us to our table. The decoration is lush, the choice of music is terrible, the acoustics is horrible, lots of echo a loud noise; they should have used sound absorbing materials on their low ceiling! Their chairs are uncomfortable with an 88 degree inclined back! As we sat on the table, they instantly gave us their nice menu, but took AGES to come back and take the order. We ordered 2x regular Entrecote formulas medium/well. For the salad you have a choice between lemon or vinegar sauce. The service was fast, they served us the walnut salads, they were good but not as refreshing and tasty as the one from Le Relais. The walnuts were cut into very small pieces bigger chunks are easier to catch! When they took the salads plates away, they place in front of us a big plate for the next meal, my plate was not properly cleaned, and had dried chunks on it! Then came 1 portion of the entrecote meat, the waiter asked us if it was 1 portion for the 2 of us, we told him that we ordered 2. They took back the tray, and came back later with 2 meat portions in 1 tray, annoyingly with very little sauce to scoop. Both meats were not medium/well as we ordered them, one was close to well done, and the other one was burned and supper well done. As we mentioned it, they apologised and replaced the burned meat with a perfect medium/well meat and lots of sauce. The quality of the meat is very good and soft, and the portion is generous. The sauce is heavy, greasy, tastes good with a kick to it, but not as good, lightly textured and refined as the one from Le Relais. Halfway through our meal, we noticed that they did not serve us bread (a tradition in Entrecôte style restaurants), we asked about it, they apologised for forgetting, and quickly served us a basked of baguette cuts that were fresh and tasted good. The big crime comes with their french fries, called “pommes frites” in the menu. They are very basic Frozen fries, the worst kind, not even home made. We had a couple of fries and left them on the plate as they did not taste good and we felt cheated. It is a BIG insult to serve frozen fries at a so called Entrecote type restaurant. If you are too lazy to prepare and cook real home made fries, don’t open a restaurant! Especially when you only serve 3 things: salad, meat and fries!!! They should all be perfect! FROZEN FRIES, really?!! What a disappointment! Someone was smoking indoor on the table next to us! It shouldn’t be permitted. They have an outdoor section, and should encourage smokers to sit outside. The look, accent, gesture and behaviour of the waiters is acceptable, but not to the standing of a french restaurant, not elegant/lush/frenchy, nothing close to the service at Le Relais. For someone who rarely eats meat and hasn’t tried the real chain Le Relais de l’Entrecote, they might like the place where you get a salad, a steak and fries for only 26$! But for a more experienced Entrecote fan, with a fine taste, this restaurant is as good as the SwissButter chain (but double its price, as the formula at SwissButter is around 12/14$), but not as good and refined as Le Relais de l’Entrecote (30$ formula). Will i come back? No. I’d rather pay an extra 4$ and go to le Relais de l’Entrecote. Or occasionally go to SwissButter, that tastes as good as Au Pirate, but with half the price and better french fries. Service: Dine in Meal type: Dinner Food: 3 Service: 3 Atmosphere: 3

I opted for the garlic bread to start which ended up almost being a small meal in itself - large pieces of thick bread with melted cheese on top. It was really tasty as well as being served quickly and hot. The main mixed grill dish was also large, with four skewers of meat, bread, veg and chips. Again, cooked really well, flavoursome and hot.Although it’s on a quiet street there was still enough happening to make sitting outside interesting and there’s wifi available if you need. review_text: [1.0] [8 months ago on Google]: باختصار تم النصب علينا و استغلال السايح الخليجي Disappointing Experience at [ Le Petit caffe ] – Poor Management and Dishonest Billing I recently visited [Le Petit caffe] with a group of six friends around 11 PM, drawn in by the inviting ambiance and bustling crowd. The café’s decor was appealing, and we were initially excited to enjoy some desserts and shisha (hookah). Our server, Ali, was a highlight of the evening—friendly, attentive, and professional, making us feel welcomed from the start. Unfortunately, our experience took a sharp downturn due to the behavior of the manager, Ahmed, and a frustrating billing issue that left us feeling deceived. Upon arrival, Ahmed informed us of a $50 minimum charge per person, which we found steep but reluctantly agreed to, as we were eager to enjoy our evening. We clearly stated that we only wanted desserts and shisha, assuming this minimum charge would cover our order. When the bill arrived, we were shocked to see a total of $327, despite our expectation of a $300 bill based on the agreed $50 per person for six people. When we questioned this, Ahmed claimed that the shisha was excluded from the minimum charge—a detail he conveniently failed to mention when we were seated. This lack of transparency felt like a deliberate attempt to inflate the bill, leaving us with a bitter taste of being scammed. The manager’s attitude was equally disappointing. He was dismissive, rude, and showed no respect for our concerns, refusing to clarify the billing discrepancy or offer a resolution. This starkly contrasted with Ali’s excellent service and soured what could have been a pleasant night out. While the café’s atmosphere and our server’s kindness were positives, the manager’s unprofessional conduct and deceptive billing practices ruined the experience. I strongly advise potential customers to clarify all charges upfront and approach with caution to avoid being overcharged. We won’t be returning Service: Dine in Meal type: Other Food: 3 Service: 1 Atmosphere: 3

review_text: [1.0] [7 years ago on Facebook]: I had to go and try Vecchio and Little Italy after his respectable owner paid me a visit at my guesthouse. It is a nice try to introduce italian cuisine to Zahle but must say it needs a lot of improvements (Just beeing diplomatic not to use other words). Let me start by thanking him for introducing me to 2 concepts which have nothing italian other than the names (Vecchio and Little Italy). Let me start with the look and feel of the place, I do not know if this place was a spanish bodega, a lebanese house, a mix of italian gastro restaurant with a tratoria or a pub. Maybe they wanted to mix everything together but I can just say I do not know what it was and definetly the look and feel is not succesfull it is more of an "International" aka as "un peu de tout" restaurant than Italian. For the food, please do not try the ham pizza, the ham quality is secondary maybe for budget constraint they had to use a ham which is not from a pork jambon but more of a mixed ham of different quality then a tip put the ham raw once the pizza went out of the oven, the ham is already cooked so no need to re cooked it again. No comment on the dough... If the objective was to create an American/australian/lebanese pizza dough then it is a success but it has nothing italian in it. I think they have just used a receipie of a mankouche dough and a pizza hut dough. Tried the "moules" not fresh and what does the moules have to do in a city at 950 m altitude with Zahleh. The best was to sticks to ingredients that people in the city appreciate like lamb and beef. For drinks cocktails are good but nothing italian u can find vodka and redbull, Sangria which is Spanish by the way and not Italian and cheap local beers not a single italian beer BUT I do not think there is demand for Italian beers in Zahleh and forgot to mention no Proseco and a very limited choice of Italian wine dommage for an Italian restaurant. The Italian wine selection is crap compared to the Lebanese wines. In a nutshell, these 2 places (Vecchio and Little Italy) are lost in translation in terms of Ambiance, foods and drinks so if you just need another "international" restaurant experience in Zahle you are fine, this place just needs to add Falafel with ciabbata bread and it will be the cherry on the cake... Burgers in an Italian restaurant that is a total turnoff not even tasty. Prices are correct reflecting the mediocre freshness of the ingredients

review_text: [4.5] [9 years ago on Zomato]: I tried Madame Tussaud's for the 1st time on a Tuesday and there was a band playing for its audience and their sound was not typical at all, playing classic rock tunes among other genres. On this particular midweek night, these two partnered locales were the only ones vibrant with life, and the place was filled with people young and old alike. The little elements of nature give life to the clear cut white tables and add some romance. The signature cocktails also have their share of green and are served in tiki inspired glasses. We ordered the Jasmin that contained coconut rum, spiced rum, passion fruit, cherry and apricot brandy, syrup, orange and cranberry juice. That was my drink and it is to die for especially if you prefer sweet drinks. If your taste buds are satisfied with sour drinks, try the Plume with white rum, dark rum, grand marnier, orange, grenadine and lemon juice with cinnamon, syrup and passion fruit. The Spinach and Artichoke Dip is an appetizer that is served with both white and brown bread and is a mixture of spinach and artichoke with creamy sauce. The cream is subtle and doesn’t overshadow the taste of the veggies, and the dish is meant to be shared and can even be split into three ways because of the generous and filling portion. I only recently started developing a taste for goat cheese, and I didn’t hesitate to order the Goat and Ricotta Cheese Salad. It is the perfect balance of sweet and sour with rocca, strawberries, apple, cherry tomato, balsamic sauce, cheesy bread and raspberry dressing. A strange yet delicious combination, I highly recommend you try this salad. The Jamaican Chicken is marinated grilled chicken with creamy coconut and mango chutney sauce served with rice. I am usually attracted to menu items that have mango, but more times than not I am disappointed when I find that the mango is nonexistent. This case is the complete opposite, where the chicken bathed on the creamy mango, I was literally drinking spoonfuls of the sauce. A staple in any dinner is the Beef Medallion, served with creamy mashed potatoes, filled artichoke, melted cheese and gravy sauce. I ordered the steak medium well to avoid overcooking, and enjoyed each bite with the sauce and potatoes. No meal is complete without dessert, so I chose the Blueberry Fondant which is also generous enough to be shared as are all their dishes. The chocolate is heavenly when combined with the tangy berries and vanilla ice cream. Madame Tussaud’s is a must try new concept with creative and delicious dishes. The portions are large, the food is fresh, and the cuisine is original. The prices are average, and if you want to compare them to other similar types of restaurants, you get much more than what you pay for. If you want to venture into new culinary journeys, then this is the place to start, you won’t be disappointed and you’re guaranteed to be coming back for more.

review_text: [5.0] [9 years ago on Zomato]: Madame Tussauds is a restaurant situated in the heart of Byblos old souk. Upon arrival you are welcomed by a magnificent setting, a delightful marriage of antique cut stones and the luxuries of modernity. Wooden white chairs and classy tables. The menu offers a wide variety of mouth-watering starters. I had the Tempura a mix of fried shrimps and crab accompanied by a delicious sauce, fried brie and the Madame Tussauds salad they were exquisite. The main course consisted of the beef medallion, while my friend had the Wok Toss beef which really thrilled us. It all was followed by the almighty halva fondant tart. All the products were fresh and the dishes had the warmth of home-made food. The restaurant also caters for all tastes by providing a large selection of tasty signature cocktails. The service also reflect the high quality of the cooking. The waiters were always smiling and the manager is always around willing to exchange some kind words with all of his clients. I had a pleasant dining experience with food of the most exquisite flavors. For this reason I highly recommend going to the Madame Tussauds restaurant.

review_text: [5.0] [5 years ago on Zomato]: ? We were invited to a sea food restaurant called Malak El Baher that was newly added to Zomato so we didn’t know what to expect, here is our review: ? We headed to Jbeil having only seen a few photos of the plates. When we got there we weren't sure it was the right place, the place seemed humble compared to the photos of the plates, but never judge a book by its cover! Even as we entered, there was an open kitchen design and no smell of fish. ?‍? Jose introduces himself as the owner & chef and went ahead to name us what he will be serving with SO much passion. He shared the story behind the restaurant, how he was the manager at Sultan Ibrahim before opening his own restaurant 3 years ago, and how everything is DAILY sourced, fresh from the Mediterranean (which explained the no-fish smell). ? The Food: ? We started out with fattoush. The attention to details and quality was obvious, you could feel the freshness of all the vegetables and even the molasses was not the commercial store-bought ones. ? We followed up with the Shrimp Hommos, Shrimp Provençal, Fried Fish in Soya and Fried Calamari. The quality of the seafood was first-class. ? The hommos itself was good, and with the added shrimp was very enjoyable, especially with the just made provençal sauce (Jose even made an extra batch at the end to for my liking ?). ? The fish with soya melts in the mouth (p.s. Pretty salty taste it at the end) ? The calamari was one of the best I've tasted because of the spices Jose had added, and freshly made tartar. ? Then came the big fish, and it made the whole trip worth it. It had no smell, was juicy and full of flavor. Even though we were full we ate it all as the taste was something else. This fish was definitely the cherry on top, a must try, a example of how fresh high quality locally sourced and passionately made food can break any conceptions you've had, and Jose should definitely be visited!

Sakhr Azar didn't just rebuild; he breathed life back into a forgotten space, weaving a story of resilience and beauty. The 'before' and 'after' photos demonstrate an extraordinary evolution, a five-year journey from crumbling stone to a three-story masterpiece. Mamaz Kitchen, the culinary heart below, delivered an experience that resonated on every level of culinary artistry and hospitality. I had the extraordinary opportunity to dine there before the official opening, and it was... perfect. Truly. Not just the food, which was exceptional, but the whole experience. The delicate aroma of expertly crafted dishes, the seamless flow of attentive service, the visual poetry of each plate – it was a sensory immersion, a triumph of restoration and refinement. And the rooms above! The breathtaking use of marble in every bathroom is a testament to the hotel's meticulous attention to detail. The staff anticipated every need, the atmosphere was magical, and you could feel the passion that went into every detail. And speaking of passion, I must mention Ms. Keyrouz, one of the managers. Her delicate touch and genuine dedication to her work were evident in every interaction. Finally: LOST is a testament to what's possible when vision meets artistry. review_text: [3.0] [a month ago on Google]: Norai offers a genuinely enjoyable dining experience, starting with the atmosphere. The space is warm, stylish, and invitingeasily one of those places where you feel comfortable lingering rather than rushing through a meal. The service matches the ambiance: attentive without being intrusive, friendly, and genuinely helpful. The staff does an excellent job when it comes to recommendations, guiding you through the menu in a way that feels thoughtful rather than scripted. One of the standout aspects of Norai is the presentation of the food. Visually, the dishes are a step above most Indian restaurants I’ve been to. Each plate is well-composed, modern, and clearly given care, making the experience feel elevated from the moment the food arrives at the table. The only real critique is in the flavor profile. While the food is good, it falls a bit short when it comes to the bold, authentic flavors traditionally associated with Indian cuisine. The seasoning and depth seem slightly toned down. This may be an intentional adjustment for the local market, though that’s just my speculation. Overall, Norai excels in atmosphere, service, and presentation. With a bit more intensity and authenticity in flavor, it could easily move from good to excellent. Food: 3 Service: 4 Atmosphere: 4

review_text: [5.0] [2 years ago on Google]: I took my husband here for his birthday. Due to the economic situation we spend months apart. When we want to go somewhere special we normally choose Beirut. My husband mentioned an Asian/Indian restaurant in Bramieh and the location was convenient. To start off the interior is gorgeous. The chairs and booths are nice quality leather and there is a painting on the wall that you would see in a magazine. We ordered dynamite shrimp as an appetizer and then Mongolian beef, chicken tikka masala and Chinese noodles for entrees. The flavor was fantastic. The rice was cooked well and no gristly pieces in the meat like you normally have from lower quality restaurants. For flavor 10:10. The portion size was slightly smaller than expected but we left satisfied. For service, I forget our waiters name unfortunately but he presented the restaurant with pride. When he explained the dishes it was as if he knew every spice and flavor. It’s rare to get service and hospitality at this level anymore. When we finished our meals, he brought a bowl of small spheres and poured water over them and they grew to moist wipes. The aroma was either rose water or orange blossom water and was very pleasant and refreshing. Finally, we were presented with the tea box. Again, he explained in detail every ingredient and their holistic benefit. He embodied the experience by incorporating taste, scent, and touch. We were honestly wowed. Thank you, Norai for giving us a lovely experience so close to home.

review_text: [4.0] [a year ago on Google]: Odette's taqueria a place I've heard about so many times through a friend. first things first, the atmosphere is very bright i really like the decor, the colors reminds me a lot of mexico. the service was great, staff was friendly and it was quite fast to be fair. I got the chance to try it, just a couple of weeks ago. and to be fair i don't want to say that the place is not good as it actually very tasty!!! however i would still want to say that this is not an authentic mexican taqueria (as i've lived in mexico). Let's first start with what they call esquites, the corn esquite is definitely not made like this as there's no such things as cherry tomatoes or avocados in it additionally crema is definitely one of the ingredients. esquites has way less ingredients (some of them cannot be find in Lebanon which is quite understandable). Secondly let's speak about the tacos, i remember having the brisket, pollo pibil (which is more common to be made with pork in mexico), the al pastor, the quesabirria and the baja fish. to be totally honest with you I LIKED ALL OF THEM (YES EVEN THE ESQUITES) even tho it's not 100% authentic and there's some ingredients missing which is quite understanble as if they were going to import everything the price of the taco would end up being the double (mostly the chiles and the corn flour to make corn tortillas). I would say that the most authentic taco (as the closest you can get to mexico) was definitely the baja. another thing, your churros should be improved cook them more and add cinnamon to the sugar, your cajeta is definitely not cajeta (it's too liquid) aand i didn't really like the chocolate dip. just do dulce de leche instead it would be better. Now one thing is sure this place has the best taqueria in the country and the closest you can get to mexico, i will definitely come back when i'll be around lebanon. Service: Dine in Meal type: Dinner Food: 4 Service: 5 Atmosphere: 5 Recommended dishes: Brisket

I told them that i can't tolerate drinking two drinks cause i have health issues, they didn't care and told me that i should immediately leave. This approach was not only aggressive but also completely inappropriate. As a paying customer, I should have the freedom to choose what and how much I want to drink without feeling pressured or coerced. Furthermore, I believe that every individual should be able to enjoy their time at a bar at their own pace, without being forced to adhere to arbitrary drink quotas. This policy is not only disrespectful but also creates an uncomfortable and unwelcoming atmosphere for patrons. I had hoped for a pleasant evening at Om Barroom, especially that i live abroad and my friends recommended the place. But unfortunately, my experience was tarnished by the rude and pushy behavior of the waitstaff. I would caution others who are seeking a relaxed and enjoyable night out to consider alternative options where they will be treated with respect and courtesy.

review_text: [4.0] [7 years ago on Zomato]: The venue is eye catching and definitely filling a unique niche in Beirut. The service is excellent and There s a proper bar, so whether you come for dinner or just drinks patois can cater to you! DO TRY: the chicken wings. YUM. All my dining companions and I concurred these are the best wings we've had in Beirut. They aren't deep fried crunchy like other places and they aren't drenched in sauce. They are juicy, flavourful and delicious. Try them! NO NEED FOR: the coconut shrimp. There are coconut flakes incorporated right into the batter, which was nice but there was something about the balance of flavours that wasn't perfect for me. I think there could be more coconut and the batter recipe can be modified so it doesn't slip off the shrimp quite so easily..still ok though! The kale Cesar salad was quite good too, the unconventional pineapple providing welcome flavour to the dish. I would say that the kale could be massaged a little more to have a smoother texture. Patois does have a 5 Islands adaptation of the long island, which will probably be loved by rum fans. Personally, I am not a fan of spiced rum and preferred the classic but the bartender knows his drinks and mixes well! Overall portions were great and the vibe is quite special. Even the music was on point. I would go back!

What I love about the sandwich is that it has its own original twist. The bread was soft but also crunchy at the same time. Let me tell you something, if you're looking for a slice of New York's little Italy, or even Italia itself, then Phil and Will is your place to go. review_text: [4.0] [a year ago on Google]: Highly Recommended Unique Gourmet Pizzas with Unusual Fine flavors, Recipies. A Must Try! This is the 2nd time i go to PizzaWa, a first one to their New Bigger Location (the 1st location closed). They introduced new meals on the menu: new starters, a cheeseburger, steak & Fries, Chicken Escalope, The Decor and ambiance are amazing, the staff is professional and welcoming, the service is fast, the presentation and quality of ingredients used are Mind Blowing, prices are affordable. For Starters we had the Oregano Foccaccia, which was good. the remarquable Eggplant Chips, and the 1923 Pizza (Caesar Salad Pizza) that was unique and Delicious!!!!!!! For the Main Course, we had the Schnitzel giant chicken escalope with a sort of caesar salad on top of it, the Best Escalope i had so far! The side fries were Very salty and of that good frozen type, but i wish they did home made fries!!!! We had the Tripper Steak & « Very Salty » Fries, which was the Biggest disappointment of the day, the steak was ok but Sadly Very Small for 29.5$!!! Check the photo! I have had more flavorful and bigger steaks in other places. It could at least have been 1.5 or 2 times bigger for a start! We also had the Nightcap & Piggy Pizzas that were very good. And for Dessert, the MerryCream, which was good but not part of the best ones i had. The other disappointment to All on the table, was the size of their pizzas, which is Small, ridiculous size for an 18 to 33$ pizza!! Check the photo! The restaurant claims that they have the same weight of a normal big pizza, we are not convinced! I understand that for a fine gourmet pizza, the classic expected size could be too big, and some people never finish their standard pizza, but this Tiny size could come as a big shock & disappointment for someone hungry and expecting a traditional size! Either lower their price and mention Small Size on the menu, or increase the size halfway from the actual to the standard « norm » size! Don’t get me wrong, the place is amazing, highly recommended. My only objection is to the Small pizza size, the salty frozen fries, and the Tiny Beef Steak size. It would be great if they could add to the menu a small choice of fine Pasta/Risotto, then it would be complete! You will not find traditional pizza at PizzaWa (marguerita, Buffala, Peperoni, 4 cheese, prosciutto y Funghi,). Only Unique Fine Deli Pizzas that will blow your mind. But to my taste, it’s the kind of place you occasionally go to, while i could go anytime to a fine traditional Italian restaurant! Where i would find All the Traditional Pizza and Pasta, that we have been used to crave for. Well done PizzaWa on your unique recipies and fine quality. Meal type: Lunch Food: 4 Service: 5 Atmosphere: 5

["Exorbitant Prices and Slow Service Mar Otherwise Promising Venue"] The venue boasts a commendable location, strategically positioned near the highway in northern Lebanon, not far from the city of Batroun. They offer an electric cart service to transport guests from the entrance to the beach, where an array of comfortable tables and chairs are available. The service, albeit courteous, is noticeably slow. The DJ requires a considerable amount of time to play invigorating music; initially, the music was exceedingly monotonous, only improving after 10:00 PM when livelier tunes finally emerged. Unfortunately, by this time, a significant portion of my friends had already left, disheartened by the earlier dull atmosphere. 

The food, while decent, is exorbitantly priced. A bottle of gin, which typically costs $25, was outrageously marked up to $128. Our modest consumption of some snacks and soft drinks, along with the gin, culminated in a staggering bill of $462. The pricing is egregiously inflated, posing a severe detriment to tourism. In numerous other countries with far superior infrastructure (such as roads, cleanliness, and service) — like Spain, France, Italy, Greece, Kazakhstan, and even Dubai — the maximum expenditure per person, including excellent food and beverages, would be approximately $40. Adding insult to injury, the valet parking demanded an additional $5.50 as a fee. In many countries, parking is complimentary when dining at a restaurant.

In Lebanon, it seems exploitation is rampant, extending beyond just the banks and political system. I intend to boycott all restaurants and pubs this summer and strongly urge others to do the same to compel these establishments to reevaluate their prices and cease their exploitative practices.

[Rude Service and Poor Quality at Oysters – Never Again] I had a very disappointing experience at Oysters this year. We ordered grilled calamari and were served only the tentacles instead of the actual calamari, which absolutely did not match the price. When we complained, both the waiter and the manager were extremely rude, insisting “this is how we serve it.” We even showed them the restaurant’s own Instagram photos, which clearly showed a completely different dish, but the manager dismissed us by saying those pictures are just for advertising.

I visited Oysters back in 2023 and had a wonderful experience — but this time, it was the complete opposite. The fish were tasteless, the fried shrimps were served with the heads and not cleaned properly, and the calamari was a total disaster. Not only did they refuse to apologize, but the manager was unprofessional, impolite, and even threw some unnecessary words at us before walking away.

We didn’t mind paying for the dish, but we simply didn’t want it. Instead of handling the situation with professionalism, the management’s attitude made everything worse. Honestly, this visit wasn’t even worth one star.

[IF IN BATROUN AND YOU SEE A RESTAURANT CALLED OYSTERS THST LOOKS SO INVITING FOR A SUNSET, DO NOT GO THERE!] My last night in Lebanon, I go to watch the sunset and see this charming seafood place called Oysters near St Estephan Church.
I ask for oysters, the one server who spoke English said they didn’t have any, then said he would check. 10 minutes later he says yes, they have 6. I’ve eaten oysters all over the world and this place looked safe…..but it is NOT.
The oysters looked funny and had a white substance dripping off them. The server told me it was “the sauce they put on them”. Sauce? What? So I tried one with the least milky stuff on it and it tasted rancid. I spit it out into a napkin. 
I told the staff they are bad, and these were likely sitting out for hours.
They insisted I had to pay, and get this, they were 5 USDs an oyster!!! No oysters in the US are that expensive.
I was told to wait for the owner. 30 minutes later he walks up and I explained what happened. The 2 servers who served me ran off in their car. Apparently another oyster was missing. I swore I did not even eat the one and spit it out. 
He told me there was nothing he could do, he must pay for each oyster. I told him if he went to a restaurant and the food was bad, would he pay? He said “Of course”
WRONG!!!!
AVOID THIS PLACE! Maybe I was naive and stupid to try and eat oysters in Lebanon, but I have eaten many places and should’ve really been more careful, but just as a warning to others….DO NOT EAT HERE!
I usually write good reviews, but this could be one of my worst ones ever!

review_text:
[BEST SEAFOOD IN BATROUN!] This seafood restaurant stood out as a culinary revelation that defied our expectations. Despite initially being overshadowed by a couple of other higher-ranked seafood restaurants in the area, we decided to give Bistr’eau a try as our first meal, upon arriving in Batroun. Little did we know, it would turn out to be the culinary highlight of our stay, ultimately the place we selected as our last meal and the grand finale of our time in Batroun.

Situated beneath a series of picturesque succession of ornate arches along the waterfront, within one of Batroun's historical buildings at the port of the Batroûn Old Souk, this restaurant stood out as a true outlier. What made this dining experience truly exceptional was the symphony of flavors orchestrated by the fusion of cuisines, the inventive pairing of traditional and rarely-used ingredients, and the meticulous execution of each dish. Between our two visits, we embarked on a culinary journey through almost the entire menu, relishing every morsel.

The appetizers alone were a testament to the culinary prowess at play – from the refreshing Fattouch to the innovative Hummus with shrimp, the smoky allure of the aubergine with sundried tomato tarator, and fresh zaatar. The culinary exploration continued with Grilled Calamari, Sicilian octopus, shrimp fokhara with tomato sauce, and perfectly roasted Patatas Bravas. All this food only served to pave the way for the triumphant main courses—seafood risotto and the pièce de résistance, a perfectly seasoned deep-fried whole fish. The culinary symphony reached its crescendo with the Pain Perdu à la mode, offering the perfect sweet note to conclude our culinary odyssey.

review_text:
[At Ibn Battuta mall] Located in Ibn Battuta mall, we visited this beautiful restaurant for late lunch. The red and white theme of the restaurant interior gives it a bright and vibrant look. Felt a very positive vibes the moment we entered the restaurant.

We started with the Functional Juices and both were very refreshing & Heavenly in taste. Start your meals with these, highly recomended. Rise and shine which is a blend of Oats, Honey, Yougurt, Berries & Bananna. Made well without excess sweet and healthy. Kale & Pineapple with is Kale, Mango, Spinach & Pineapple. This has good health benefits for those who are looking for healthy options.

Mushroom Soup was very nice consistency and very thick. We loved the taste of the spices mixed with it. The Burratta salad is no doubt another best seller. Freshly made Burratta cheese which was very soft and tasty.

Grilled shrimp skewers on a bed of Sauteed veggies is another fantastic dish. The shrimps do not smell cause the marination is perfect and we get the taste of the mild marination spices mixed with shrimps. The Turkey Club Sandwitch is another killer. Taste of the Eggs with Veggies inside is superb. Grilled salmon with Quinoa was very well done and the Salmon did not smell strong but instead we can feel the taste in our mouths. Usually a strong smell of the Salmon is a out off, so the Chef has handled this very nicely. A must have for Salmon lovers.

The Apple and Celery drink is another superb drink. All the shakes and Smoothies are made by Mary Jane a trained expert in juices.

The Strawberry Pistachio Cheesecake was the one we selected from their display of mouth watering Desserts. The tangy sauce with the sweetness underneath was a riot of taste in our taste buds. Later we had their Pistachio & Caramel Ice Creams. All these Desserts are a must have to satiate your cravings.

The restaurant supervisor Mary Jane deserve a special mention, her mannerisms and knowledge about the food were praiseworthy.

Overall we had a great experience here. Service is good. Taste, quality and presentation of the food is praiseworthy.

review_text:
[Brunch in style right where you’re seated at!] Journey:
We were invited to try out thier new brunch at the Mirdiff branch. Since, brunches and fridays go hand in hand in Dubai so we could not wait to experience it for ourselves.

Ambiance:
The moment you make your way towards LOL, you have a coffee & tea counter setup, where you can have a brew of your choice and right next to them are thier delicious pastries lined up. There is a casual vibe and the dim lighting to enjoy your weekend. The seating is comfy which includes couches and chairs. It is perfect either way if you are part of a large group or planning a small affair, the cafe will suit your needs.

Rating: 7.5 Golden Nuggets

Bite Board

LOL launched a new concept for the brunch where the food comes to you instead of you walking around in circles deciding what to eat. Also, it is an unlimited brunch where you can keep refilling your plates with servings of the dish you like. The brunch is priced at AED 79 and is available on Fridays and Saturdays.

Drinks: There are options for strawberry and peach lemonade, fresh orange juice and water. We tried the orange juice and strawberry lemonade. Both the drinks were refreshing.

French Toast & Pancakes: A well-cooked french toast with a dash of cinnamon and topped with fresh berries served along with maple syrup. It was our favorite dish that we could not help ourselves from a second serving, YES THAT GOOD! The pancakes were fluffy and topped with raspberry sauce but were dry texture wise.

Choice of Eggs: There are two options where you could choose between a scrambled/boiled/fried egg or a mushroom omelette. We went for a scrambled egg that was served on top of a sourdough bread.

Breakfast Rosti: A platter with chili chickpeas, bacon, cherry tomatoes, mushrooms, roasted potatoes and sausages. Our friend was a huge fan of the chickpeas dish as it was something different and had an amazing flavor to it.

Red Quinoa Salad: The combination of beetroot and quinoa was superb. Usually, we are not huge fans of quinoa but this totally changed our minds and we would not mind a repeat of it.

Moutabal: We could not taste this as there were no breads along with it. Our suggestion would be to add some arabic bread or bread-sticks in the future.

Tunisian Chicken Meatballs: A bit different from the regular meatballs which usually involves red meat. These chicken meatballs had the right amount of spices and were cooked perfectly.

Prawn Penne Arrabbiata: Since our friend was a vegetarian, we requested for the pasta without the prawns. The pasta was cooked well but we would have preferred the tomatoes to be slightly less, guess its just how the dish was and does not suit our palate.

Roast Harissa Chicken: The dish would have been another one of our favorites if only the chicken was not too dry and too hard to cut through.

Desert Platter: It included carrot cake, red velvet cake and macarons. Both the cakes were soft and melted in your mouth but the macarons were a miss for us.

Service:
This is an aspect that needs to be worked on, the staff needed to be called multiple times to hear out our request.

Cash Outflow:
The price is quite reasonable for the unlimited brunch. 

Location:
26B Street, Mirdiff Park Center, Dubai

Circling Back:
We shall make another visit to try their desserts and coffee.

review_text: [Therapeutic] Menagerie's most formidable talent lies not in the expertly(and exceptionally) prepared food, the tastefully decorated interiors or its applaudable soundtrack ( playing indie-hits like Lord Huron and Janis Ian) but rather in its ability to just 'be'. It doesn't try to propagate a faux sense of ostentatiousness or boast about its approach to healthy living. In this exclusive little mall called Mirdif 35, Menagerie is a place untouched by the too-easily damaged veneer of golden consumerism that plagues 99% of tinsel Dubai. review_text:
[Delicious Koobideh kababs] Hatam __ A lovely Iranian Restaurant in Dubai! They serve complimentary bread and green salad platter that consist of rocket leaves,mint leaves,walnuts, olives,feta cheese, and pickled veggies upon arrival.

I used cobone vouchers for my meal. This cobone deal is still on. You can save upto 50% on the bill by getting the vouchers. The menu card prices available on Zomato website for this restaurant need some updating as these are different from the prices mentioned on the Menu card at the restaurant.

I had the following dishes:

Lentil soup:  It was non spicy and tasted good.

Mixed salad: Though they serve basic salad platter complimentary but this 4 in 1 platter was really good. It had hummus, mutable, tabbouleh and seasonal salad in it.

Mixed Hatam salad: consisted of  dolma, humus topped with grilled meat, feta cheese and green mix salad. Loved it!

Arayes: Arayes is a middle eastern grilled pita bread stuffed with lamb mince, onions, tomatoes and spices. It was very delicious! But they forgot to serve fries with it as it was shown in the menu card’s Arayes picture.

Kabab Koobideh:  Special Iranian kababs served with rice were very juicy and tasty. They make the best koobideh kababs!!

Tikka and kabab:  Marinated lamb pieces served with rice were nicely grilled.

Falooda:  It was very chilled and refreshing!

Overall it was a nice experience. Seating facility is good. Walls are adorned with beautiful paintings. They also have family cabins for privacy. Our server was kind and friendly. He was happy to help us when we asked him for the extra plates and cutleries. I would love to come back here again.

Tucked in the charming old town of Byblos, El Molino is a refreshing and vibrant escape that brings the bold and colorful flavors of Mexico to the Lebanese coast. From the moment you step inside, you’re greeted by warm hospitality and a festive atmosphere that blends Mexican décor with a Mediterranean twist.
The menu is thoughtfully curated, offering a range of traditional Mexican dishes—from sizzling fajitas and loaded nachos, to authentic tacos al pastor, burritos, and enchiladas. Every dish bursts with flavor and is clearly crafted with fresh, quality ingredients. One standout is the guacamole, freshly made tableside and served with crispy homemade tortilla chips. Their margaritas—especially the spicy version—are not to be missed, offering the perfect balance of heat and citrus.

Service is friendly and attentive, with staff happy to explain dishes or offer recommendations. The ambiance is lively yet cozy, ideal for both casual outings and special celebrations. Whether you’re seated indoors or enjoying the outdoor terrace, the vibe remains inviting and relaxed.

review_text: [A gem seafood restaurant in Amchit] This is a very small restaurant that is part of a fishery on the coast of Amchit north of Byblos. The fishery is well known under the name of its owner Pierre Abboud but few people know that it is also a restaurant. The place is very small (8 tables only) and there is no decoration. Actually you can’t even see it from the road because it is hidden by a tree. But the food is so good. Of course, since Pierre is a fisherman you get the catch of the day. All fresh and perfectly cooked  and seasoned. We had a selection of calamari with garlic and parsley, fried fish and broiled sole. Accompanied by hummus and fattoush. It was all delicious. Service is fast. And the surprise: prices are way cheaper than the trove of fancy seafood restaurants dotting the Byblos-Amchit coast. Definitely a hidden gem.

review_text:
[Non Traditional Breakfast with Fresh Cunchy & Stuffed Meat Sandiwches, Friendly Atmosphere, Hidden Gems of Beirut,] Background:

It was recommended by one of my friends. His father used to take him there when he was a kid. We went together with other friends and we had our sandwiches feast. It is a ''non – traditional'' Lebanese way of having breakfast.
It is not a man2oushe nor hummus and foul. 
The breakfast here is sandwiches that range from the typical labne and cheese to meat sandwiches such as sujuk (sausages), roast beef, Sawda (the kidney of the chicken) and lsenet (roasted cow tongue).

What to Expect:

It is an old sandwich shop in Beirut:
-The place is small
-seating is basic: stool and aluminum bar
-decoration is minimal. 
-Suitable for a group of friends or a take away for the family.

My own Experience:

The sandwiches I tried were roast beef, sawda and sujuk. The three were crunchy and freshly baked but more importantly stuffed with meat and hence you enjoy the real taste of the sandwich.
I loved how he adds  fresh mint for all the sandiwches

Wait for the owner to call your number and stay aware of it as he will be asking you if you want it spicy or not? with mayonnaise mustard and pickles. The owner is friendly and has his own way in interacting with customers. 

The atmospheres is nice and friendly. Standing with other people waiting for your number and accordingly for the delicious sandwiches!!! A spontaneous chat with the one next to you is unavoidable.

Recommendations:

You have three sizes of sandwiches:
-Half a sandwich (recommended) (2$)
-A medium size sandwich 
-And a large sandwich (4$)
 
 I recommend you to have othe half sandwich option and order two different sandiwches. Afte tthe two i  can assure you you will be satisfyingly FULL!!!
If you want to take it further try the desserts sandwiches which are usually served at home such as jam and halawa

Timing: it is good to go there for breakfast or brunch. He closes in the early afternoon when all the food is sold out.

How to get there: Hidden in the narrow alleys of corniche Al Mazraa. Ask the taxi to drop you next to Paindore and when you reach paindore ask anyone and they will show you. (1 min walking distance)
